articles.title: Cumbre en Londres por Nicolas Jackson
articles.standfirst: Mateu Alemany se reúne con el Chelsea en la capital británica para conseguir para el Atlético la cesión del delantero
articles.summary: Alemany intenta acelerar la cesión del delantero del Chelsea
articles.body: Con Sorloth lesionado y Julián todavía lejos de su mejor forma, el Atlético se ha lanzado para intentar cerrar la llegada de un nuevo futbolista de ataque que refuerce la delantera rojiblanca. Para ello, Mateu Alemany, director de fútbol profesional del club rojiblanco, llegó este jueves a Londres para intentar cerrar el fichaje de Nicolas Jackson. A pesar de que hay una terna con varios nombres, el delantero senegalés es, a día de hoy, una de las opciones preferentes en los despachos del Metropolitano y los rojiblancos tratan de acelerar su llegada.  Mateu Alemany, que ayer estuvo presente en el duelo del Metropolitano ante el Málaga, emprendió viaje esta mañana desde el aeropuerto de Barajas a Londres para intentar avanzar en la contratación del delantero del Chelsea. El ex del Villarreal se postula como la principal opción para la delantera rojiblanca tras una temporada cedido en Múnich. Con los límites ajustados después del refuerzo del Cuti Romero por 33 millones más 7 en variables, el Atlético busca encontrar una condiciones ventajosas que permitan lanzarse a por el senegalés. No será sencillo al encontrarse entre los pretendientes equipo con músculo económico como el Aston Villa de Emery, el míster que lo subió al primer equipo en Villarreal. El senegalés es una alternativa ante la posible salida de Olie Watkins a Arabia. “Todo es complicado. El mercado si lo ves desde fuera se ha puesto duro y cada año que pasa mas complicado porque hay mucho dinero en el sistema. Hay inflación. Los jugadores especiales son difíciles de conseguir”, aseguraba Mateu en los micrófonos de Movistar en la noche del miércoles. Y es que la situación del mercado rojiblanco obliga a los del Metropolitano a intentar una operación en forma de cesión e intentando que el Chelsea pudiese hacerse cargo de parte de la ficha del futbolista. Eso sí, el Atlético cuenta con el deseo del futbolista de regresar al fútbol español, donde ya despuntó en su ascenso al primer equipo del Villarreal. Jackson vivió unos meses frenéticos desde que debutó con el club amarillo. Tras un fichaje frustrado por el Bournemouth en el mercado invernal de esa temporada, el senegalés acabó en Londres como jugador del Chelsea por unos 37 millones. Ahora, tras dos temporadas en la Premier y una cesión en el Bayern, el Atlético intentará hacerse con sus servicios para apuntalar el ataque junto a Julián y Sorloth.

articles.standfirst: Formamos la selección con los tres aspirantes al título en el Movistar Fantasy MARCA
articles.summary: Formamos la selección con los tres aspirantes al título en el Movistar Fantasy MARCA
articles.body: No solo de las grandes estrellas vive el mánager del Movistar Fantasy MARCA, pero imprescindibles son para competir por los más de 10.000 euros en premios. Mbappé, Lamine y Julián Álvarez, los 'Three Kings' de los aspirantes al título, salen reforzados con fichajazos a golpe de talonario como Diomande, Rodri y Kang-In Lee. El surcoreano tuvo un debut soñado con los rojiblancos en LaLiga: golazo espectacular y 10 puntos en apenas media hora sobre el terreno de juego (vale 35,4 millones). Este sábado se estrena el Madrid de Mou 2.0 en el RCDE Stadium y el domingo lo hará el actual campeón en el Martínez Valero. ¿Por qué elegir si la magia del Fantasy nos permite juntar? Tirando de los 400 millones de la Jornada Movistar montaremos el 'Dream Team' de Barça, Madrid y Atlético, pero antes de elegir no está de más comparar. En valor de plantilla se impone el Barça con 792 millones, por los 776 del Real Madrid y los sorprendentes 523 del Atlético.  El deficiente rendimiento liguero de los rojiblancos en la 25-26 nos regala algunos de los mejores chollazos en clave Fantasy: Julián Álvarez (41,3 millones), Baena (40,2), Oblak (36,6), Grimaldo (34,8) o Pablo Barrios (24,3). De hecho hay que bajar hasta el puesto 25º del ranking por valor de mercado para encontrar al primer jugador del Atlético, Lookman (41,4 millones). Dumfries (33) y Adeyemi (40) son los nuevos en Madrid y Barça con cartel de posibles chollazos. articles.title: Brent Venables, Oklahoma Reportedly Agree to New Contract, Will Be Among CFB's Highest-Paid HCs
articles.summary: Brent Venables led Oklahoma to the College Football Playoff last season and will now be with the program for the foreseeable future.
articles.body:
Brent Venables led Oklahoma to the College Football Playoff last season and will now be with the program for the foreseeable future.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Thursday the Sooners and Venables agreed to a new six-year contract that adds two years to his current deal and runs through the 2031 campaign. The contract will pay the coach an average of $10.5 million per year.

According to USA Today's database , it will make him the sixth-highest-paid coach in the sport on an annual average.

Only Georgia's Kirby Smart ($13.3 million per year), Ohio State's Ryan Day ($12.6 million), USC's Lincoln Riley ($11.5 million), Clemson's Dabo Swinney ($11.4 million) and Texas' Steve Sarkisian ($10.8 million) will be paid more.

Smart, Day and Swinney are all national-championship-winning coaches, while Riley and Sarkisian are leading two of the nation's most prominent programs in USC and Texas.

As for Venables, he helped Swinney win two national championships at Clemson as a defensive coach who was widely considered one of the best assistants in all of college football. In fact, the Tigers have struggled to remain among the nation's best since Venables left to become Oklahoma's head coach.

Yet things did not get off to an ideal start for the Sooners during his tenure, as they went 6-7 and lost in the Cheez-It Bowl in his first season. They also went 6-7 and lost the Armed Forces Bowl during his third year in 2024.

In fact, Oklahoma still hasn't won a postseason game in Venables' four years at the helm.

Still, it made notable strides last season, going from a 6-7 team to one that went 10-2 in the regular season and reached the CFP. That was largely because of the play on the defensive side of the ball, as Oklahoma was seventh in the country and first in the SEC in points allowed per game.

That Venables, who is a defensive-minded coach with a defensive background, was able to get the Sooners to play at an elite level on that side of the ball was anything but surprising.

While Oklahoma eventually lost to Alabama in the first round of the CFP, it was once again among the nation's best teams. And that is where Venables will look to help it stay during the course of his new contract extension.

articles.title: El nuevo Hjulmand con pasado en el Barça ya brilla en Europa: “Asumo la responsabilidad”
articles.standfirst: Sergi Altimira irrumpe en el Sporting de Portugal como el elegido para ocupar el vacío dejado por el nuevo fichaje del Atlético. El español, formado en el Barça y con pasado en el Betis, ya ha dejado su primera huella en Lisboa y se sincera con Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Sergi Altimira irrumpe en el Sporting de Portugal como el elegido para ocupar el vacío dejado por el nuevo fichaje del Atlético. El español, formado en el Barça y con pasado en el Betis, ya ha dejado su primera huella en Lisboa y se sincera con Radio MARCA
articles.body: Hay nuevo dueño para el centro del campo del Sporting de Portugal. Sergi Altimira llegó este verano a Lisboa procedente del Betis con una misión tan atractiva como exigente: ocupar el espacio dejado por Morten Hjulmand, el pivote danés que puso rumbo al Atlético de Madrid. El español no ha necesitado demasiado tiempo para empezar a hacerse notar: gol en sus primeros partidos, adaptación inmediata y una declaración de intenciones que resume su mentalidad ante el nuevo desafío. Y esto es solo un aperitivo. Altimira deja muchos más titulares en una entrevista en la que habla sin filtros de Hjulmand, Rodri, el Barça, el Betis y su nuevo reto en Lisboa. La entrevista completa, a partir de este sábado, en Marcador Internacional. La comparación con Hjulmand es inevitable. El danés dejó el Sporting para dar el salto al Atlético y ahora Altimira afronta el reto de hacerse con un sitio en un equipo acostumbrado a pelear por títulos. El centrocampista asume la exigencia y entiende la responsabilidad que conlleva su llegada: “Sé el club donde estoy y lo que esperan de mí”. También tiene claro el objetivo: “Todos los equipos tendrán jugadores importantes y llegan jugadores que tienen que intentar suplirlo”. En Lisboa encontrará, además, el escenario ideal para seguir creciendo: un equipo que aspira a recuperar el trono de su liga y que volverá a competir en la Champions. El Sporting llega a esta temporada con la ambición de volver a lo más alto después de que el FC Porto se proclamara campeón en la última edición del campeonato. Antes de eso, los verdiblancos habían encadenado dos títulos consecutivos, lo que muestra de la exigencia que rodea al club. La historia de Altimira tiene todos los ingredientes de una carrera construida desde abajo. Hace diez años estaba en el cadete del Barça, después pasó por el Sabadell y recorrió categorías inferiores antes de llegar al primer nivel con el Betis: “Tuve que pisar el barro, Segunda B, ir escalando poco a poco”, recuerda. Su etapa en Sevilla fue fundamental, pero el jugador entendió que había llegado el momento de dar el siguiente paso: “Noté que necesitaba salir para no estancarme”. El Sporting apareció como una oportunidad para competir por títulos y, sobre todo, para estrenarse en el gran escenario europeo. Altimira también habla de Rodri, una referencia natural para cualquier pivote español. El nuevo jugador del Sporting reivindica el reconocimiento al trabajo de un futbolista que, según él, no siempre recibe el protagonismo que merece: “Muchas veces pasa desapercibido, pero hace un trabajo increíble, una inteligencia táctica brutal, que al final cualquier equipo necesita”.  Y cuando le plantean si él mismo podría algún día seguir ese camino, regresar a España y hacerlo con un Balón de Oro, responde con una sonrisa y sin ponerse límites: “¿Por qué no? Un Balón de Oro hay que firmar”. La entrevista completa, este sábado en Marcador Internacional, en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Punto y final al 'culebrón' El Mala
articles.standfirst: El extremo alemán, pretendido por Dortmund y Leipzig, renueva por el Colonia
articles.summary: El extremo alemán, pretendido por Dortmund y Leipzig, renueva por el Colonia
articles.body: El nombre que más titulares ha copado a lo largo del verano no juega en Bayern Múnich, Borussia Dortmund, RB Leipzig... Es Said El Mala y ha protagonizado un auténtico 'culebrón' que, en principio, ya tiene resolución: ha renovado con el Colonia. Su ausencia en la lista de Alemania para el Mundial 2026 generó un auténtico cisma en el país después de consagrarse como una de las grandes revelaciones de la Bundesliga con 13 goles y cuatro asistencias. Un rendimiento que nadie podía esperar cuando, un año antes, se encontraba cedido en el Viktoria Köln de Tercera división. "El futuro de Said llegará pronto. Pero claro, se lo habría merecido, por eso estas conversaciones son difíciles", dijo Nagelsmann. No le faltaban novias. El Leipzig fue uno de los primeros equipos en mostrar interés... pero quien más fuerte se lanzó a por sus servicios fue el Borussia Dortmund. Ole Book tenía su nombre señalado en rojo para ocupar el sector izquierdo del ataque de Niko Kovac. "No hablamos de jugadores que no sean del Borussia Dortmund", se limitaba a pronunciar el director deportivo del conjunto 'borussen'. En Alemania, sin embargo, se han telegrafiado unas negociaciones que a inicios de semana, presuntamente, terminaron de colapsar. Tal y como se informó en Sky Sports, el Colonia exigía 50 millones para dejar salir a El Mala. Una cifra a la que el Borussia Dortmund no estaba dispuesto a llegar. Para hacernos una idea, la venta más cara en la historia del Colonia fue la de Modeste al fútbol chino en 2019 por 29 millones. Escasos días después, el club ha anunciado la renovación de su contrato por una temporada más —hasta 2031— y le ha entregado el dorsal '10' de Podolski de cara al próximo curso. "Desde que estoy aquí, el Colonia me ha dado muy buenas sensaciones cada día. Es increíblemente divertido trabajar con estos compañeros y cuerpo técnico", expresó. El Mala, sin embargo, no escondió sus intenciones de 'volar' lejos del Colonia. "Mi primera temporada en la Bundesliga aquí fue muy especial. Y, por supuesto, después pensé en mi futuro. Siento una enorme confianza y un gran aprecio aquí. Por eso me quedo: quiero tener una buena temporada y lo daré todo por ello, también porque sé lo que significa llevar el número 10". "Estamos muy contentos de que Said continúe su trayectoria aquí. Ha progresado muchísimo la temporada pasada, se ha consolidado como una pieza clave de nuestro equipo en la Bundesliga y ha sido fundamental para nuestro equipo con sus actuaciones y goles", declaró Kessler, director deportivo del Colonia. Este 'culebrón' tendrá más capítulos. Pero ya no serán este verano.

articles.title: Oficial: Troy Parrott, nuevo jugador del Betis hasta 2031
articles.standfirst: El acuerdo con el AZ Alkmaar se cerró en 16 millones de euros, más cuatro en variables
articles.summary: El acuerdo con el AZ Alkmaar se cerró en 16 millones de euros, más cuatro en variables
articles.body: El Betis ha hecho oficial el fichaje de Troy Parrott hasta 2031. El delantero irlandés llegó este jueves a Sevilla para pasar el reconocimiento médico y firmar su nuevo contrato con los verdiblancos. La Dirección Deportiva completa la delantera y eleva la competencia en una temporada exigente e ilusionante para los andaluces, que volverán a disputar la Champions League 21 años después. Así lo ha anunciado el club verdiblanco: "El Real Betis Balompié y el AZ Alkmaar han llegado a un acuerdo para el traspaso del jugador Troy Parrott. El delantero internacional irlandés se convierte en el cuarto refuerzo verdiblanco de este verano y firma hasta 2031. Troy Parrott (Dublín, 4 de febrero de 2002) comenzó su carrera deportiva en el Belvedere FC de Irlanda, de donde salió al juvenil del Tottenham en 2017. Tras varias cesiones en Inglaterra en Millwall, Ipswich, MK Dons y Preston, llegó su salto a la Eredivisie de Países Bajos, militando en el Excelsior y el AZ Alkmaar, club del que procede. El nuevo delantero verdiblanco llega tras sumar 31 goles y 12 asistencias en la última temporada con el conjunto neerlandés, donde se alzó con la Copa y Supercopa de los Países Bajos. Parrott es también un fijo con la selección de Irlanda, sumando 37 internacionalidades y 11 goles".

articles.title: Otra vez Mariano
articles.standfirst: Por primera vez en sus nueve temporadas en el fútbol español, el ex del Real Madrid encadena dos jornadas consecutivas viendo portería.
articles.summary: Por primera vez en sus nueve temporadas en el fútbol español, el ex del Real Madrid encadena dos jornadas consecutivas viendo portería.
articles.body: Mariano va muy en serio. Al igual que en la primera jornada ante el Getafe, el delantero volvió a ser decisivo para que el Alavés rescatara un punto en su visita a Butarque. En la recta final, cuando parecía que los puntos iban a quedarse en la capital, el ‘9’ estuvo más listo que nadie para aprovechar una cesión errónea de Ratiu para plantarse solo delante de Cárdenas y batirle con un disparo raso.   Su exhibición en el estreno liguero no fue suficiente para que fuera titular, ya que Quique Sánchez Flores se decantó por situar a Lucas Boyé al lado de Toni Martínez. Sin embargo, el preparador madrileño recurrió al ariete hispano-dominicano cuando el encuentro se había puesto cuesta arriba con el tanto de Camello. Y su apuesta por Mariano volvió a tener recompensa en forma de gol.  El delantero sacó a relucir su cara más certera para ser determinante en Butarque. En un contexto menos favorable, sin tantos espacios para explotar su velocidad como contra el Getafe, pero mostrando su versión más efectiva para marcar en una de las pocas acciones que dispuso. El ‘9’ pudo completar la remontada en el descuento con un disparo desde la frontal que atajó sin problemas Cárdenas.  Pese a ello, la actuación del ex del Real Madrid fue por segunda jornada consecutiva fundamental en el devenir del partido. En apenas cuatro días, Mariano ha pasado de encadenar más de cuatro años sin marcar un gol en Liga a encadenar dos encuentros seguidos viendo puerta, algo que no había sido capaz de hacer en las anteriores ocho temporadas en el fútbol español. El delantero habló al final del encuentro. "Los comentarios hago que no me afecten. Espero que haya vuelto el mejor Mariano y que esta versión pueda continuar", afirmó. El inicio de curso de Mariano está superando las expectativas y Quique está sabiendo reconducir a un jugador que por fin ha encontrado la salida del laberinto en el que se encontraba en las últimas temporadas. Tanto es así que el ‘9’ ha participado de forma directa en los cuatro goles que ha hecho el Alavés en el arranque liguero –dos goles y dos asistencias–. La resurrección cada vez coge más forma y ahora tendrá que darle continuidad.

El delantero habló al final del encuentro. "Los comentarios hago que no me afecten. Espero que haya vuelto el mejor Mariano y que esta versión pueda continuar", afirmó. El inicio de curso de Mariano está superando las expectativas y Quique está sabiendo reconducir a un jugador que por fin ha encontrado la salida del laberinto en el que se encontraba en las últimas temporadas. Tanto es así que el ‘9’ ha participado de forma directa en los cuatro goles que ha hecho el Alavés en el arranque liguero –dos goles y dos asistencias–. La resurrección cada vez coge más forma y ahora tendrá que darle continuidad.

articles.title: Beñat San José: "Es un plus de energía el imaginarme Vallecas lleno"
articles.standfirst: El técnico vasco habló sobre el encuentro ante el Deportivo Alavés con los medios
articles.summary: El técnico vasco habló sobre el encuentro ante el Deportivo Alavés con los medios
articles.body: El Rayo Vallecano salió de Butarque con un punto y dos bajas muy sensibles, la de Isi y la de Augusto Batalla. Beñat San José atendió a los medios de comunicación tras el encuentro y habló sobre sus sensaciones tras el empate, la lesión de Augusto Batalla y la falta de público. Sensación del partido: Tiene dos valoraciones. Hemos hecho un muy buen partido, muy completo. Hemos jugado un fútbol muy vertical en el que hemos servido todas nuestras cualidades ante un rival muy difícil. Los jugadores han estado dinámicos. Hoy nos han anulado otro gol, lo aceptamos y ya está. La otra parte ha sido que el gol de ellos ha sido una acción desafortunada nuestra y los cambios forzados. Dejas de tener dos cambios en el momento que quieres tenerlos, más luego la última ventana, nos ha pasado factura en los últimos quince minutos. Creo que tendríamos que haber sumado de tres. Lesión de Batalla: Nos ha hecho no poder hacer cambios de campo. Ha sido un partido muy accidentado. Hay que valorar cuando hemos estado todos. Batalla estaba con el doctor y todavía no me habían dado ningún informe. Identidad del equipo: Nos falta que no tengamos tantos accidentes en los partidos. En el anterior partido que si penalti, que si gol anulado...Pero estoy muy orgulloso de los jugadores que están enfocados. A veces la mente no está bien, pero mis jugadores han demostrado ser fuertes. Cuando el descanso acecha tenemos que mejorar ese control de balón. Con esas dos cosas el equipo va dar un salto hacia delante. Estoy orgulloso del foco de los jugadores. Espectadores: Nunca he puesto ninguna excusa, pero ese punto es tremendo. Agradecer de corazón a los que han venido y sentir lástima por los que no, pero los entendemos totalmente. Es un varapalo total. Es un triple esfuerzo que tenemos que hacer todos. Pero no vamos a ir con la excusa por delante. Es un plus de energía el imaginarme Vallecas lleno y por favor pido que el siguiente partido se juegue en Vallecas.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Brighton midfielder Lia Walti 'missed feeling of being valued'
articles.summary: Brighton midfielder Lia Walti said she "missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer" and craved a return to the Women's Super League.
articles.body:
Brighton midfielder Lia Walti said she "missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer" and craved a return to the Women's Super League.

The Switzerland captain left Arsenal for Juventus in 2025 but her short time in Italy exposed the stark differences between the WSL and other leagues.

Walti helped former club Arsenal win four major trophies during a seven-year spell there, including the Champions League and WSL titles.

She moved to Italy in search of a new challenge but quickly realised the differences in professionalism were "extreme".

After one season, Walti returned to England, joining ambitious WSL club Brighton last month for an undisclosed fee.

"It's such a huge difference. It's always hard to speak about it. I don't want to speak too negatively about the Italian league, that is not my aim," Walti told BBC Sport.

"It's more that it's just the reality that football in England, in the WSL, has a standard which is not comparable with any other league.

"It's a bit sad and disappointing to see a lot of girls abroad do not have the same opportunities or standards in terms of being in professional environments."

Walti said she realised the WSL's standards "are not the norm" and she missed playing in front of an established football culture.

"I missed the feeling of being valued as a footballer, feeling like we're getting the full support we needed," added Walti.

"We have good structures, good fields where we can play our games. We had absolutely no fan culture - not just at Juve - in general in Italy.

"When you have been part of that growth in England, with the fan cultures, the full stadiums - even stadiums that are really small, they are exciting to play in.

"In Italy, it was just [empty]. Every game felt a bit like that. I missed the feeling I had before when I was playing football."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Why are there so few African players in the WSL? Published 5 days ago

Why are there so few African players in the WSL?

New-look Villa turn to Scandinavia as they rebuild squad Published 6 days ago

New-look Villa turn to Scandinavia as they rebuild squad

The 33-year-old made 183 appearances for Arsenal and established herself as a key player for the club.

She captained her country at Euro 2025 on home soil and has over a century of appearances for Switzerland.

Walti's experiences have come as part of a generation that has catapulted women's football growth in England and she believes others can follow suit.

"I think you have to bring the game to the people. You kind of have to force people to watch it. I felt that that's how it maybe started in England," said Walti.

"In Italy, and in a lot of other countries, I think they have bad coverage. It's not shown [on TV] at all, or if it's shown, from where they film it, is really poor.

"It affects the way you watch a game. You don't really see the speed, the tactics or anything and you don't enjoy watching the game.

"In England, in the big stadiums, you can have great camera angles. I think people enjoy watching it more."

While the standard of coverage is a key issue according to Walti, she says there are "so many different things" that are also lacking in women's football globally.

"The biggest lacking starts with pitch quality. In a lot of countries, you play either on the worst artificial pitches or the worst natural grasses," added Walti.

"Even if a Premier League team were to play there, it would probably look rubbish because it's just not possible to play nice football on it.

"All of the other leagues, where do you even start? It's so hard. We have the same [issues] in Switzerland.

"You have to do the first step - invest money for all those things before you get something back. I think a lot of countries don't have that money or patience."

Walti said she is "passionate" about pushing for change because she is privileged to have experienced professionalism in England.

"We used to not have good conditions. It wasn't professional. Our first salaries were not enough to live from," said Walti.

"Now, seeing the growth in England and being with players who try to push the game in their own countries, it makes you feel frustrated to still see the reality.

"You forget sometimes, when you're in your own bubble, that this is not the norm. You're just one of the lucky ones who can experience it.

"A lot of talent in women's football gets lost because they are in bad environments where nobody sees them or they don't have the chance to reach their potential.

"I try to make an impact and I think that was really hard in Italy because I felt like when we spoke up, nothing happened, and that was frustrating."

When Walti was weighing up her future, with a year left on her Juventus contract, she knew Brighton were a club who could offer her a quality environment.

In April, Brighton released their plans for Europe's first purpose-built women's football stadium, which will cost Â£75-80m.

In 2021, the women's team moved into their training facilities at the American Express Elite Football Performance Centre - the result of an Â£8.5m investment.

On the pitch, they have invested during the transfer window and reached the Women's FA Cup final for the first time in May.

Dario Vidosic's side have ambitions of breaking into the WSL's top three and Walti believes she has joined a club "that cares" about women's football.

"After that experience in Italy, I knew a bit more about what I probably wanted, or didn't want," said Walti.

"I had a pretty big trust in Brighton before we had the conversations because I had been in the league and seen what the club was doing.

"I've heard from other players about the club investing a lot and I only heard really positive things. There is no better feedback than from other players.

"Once I started to have the first moments with the club, it proved to me that this is the right place - that cares about women's football, that invests in women's football, and who has the right people in place."

articles.title: Mohamed Salah: How Trabzonspor pulled off deal for ex-Liverpool forward
articles.summary: Mohamed Salah was expected to move to Saudi Arabia or the United States after leaving Liverpool, but Turkish side Trabzonspor pulled off one of the coups of the transfer window.
articles.body:
As Mohamed Salah signed his two-year deal in front of tens of thousands of fans inside Trabzonspor's Papara Park stadium, the man putting his signature to the contract next to the Egyptian was struggling to keep the smile off his face.

The reaction of supporters over the previous few days had already convinced club president Ertugrul Dogan he had pulled off a transfer coup.

"He's the biggest Muslim footballer in the world. He's an influential role model," he told BBC Sport Africa and BBC Turkish.

"We held Salah's signing ceremony in front of 35,000 people.

"It was clear from everything he did that he felt that love, and he told us as much too. He thanked us."

So how did Dogan persuade one of football's megastars to join a club without Champions League football and which has won the Turkish title only once since its heyday in the 1970s and early 1980s?

Located on the Black Sea coast, the city of Trabzon sits near the border with Georgia in the north-east corner of Turkey.

With a population of around 800,000 people, it is not even in the top 20 when it comes to the country's largest urban centres.

But Dogan claims it has something special.

"I always say this about Trabzonspor and the city - we're the biggest one-club city in the world.

"Salah asked us something like, 'Why should I choose Trabzonspor now?'

"We told him about the city and said: 'You can be sure you will meet a group of supporters unlike any you have experienced before. You'll feel the genuine love those people have inside them'."

Born in January 1977, Dogan is himself a son of Trabzon.

The businessman made his money through a series of different ventures, including real estate and hazelnuts, before moving into the energy sector and specialising in biofuels.

He became Trabzonspor president in 2023, shortly after the club's most successful season in recent memory - having won the league title in 2021-22.

Under Dogan's watch, the Black Sea Storm, as the club is known, have finished third, seventh and third in the Super Lig.

Last season they won the Turkish Cup under coach Fatih Tekke, who is now looking to guide his team into the Europa League, despite a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg of their play-off tie against Hungary's Ferencvaros.

"We are working to make Trabzonspor and Trabzon itself a destination for talented young players from all over the world," said Dogan.

"We want to take them to the next level, to move on to bigger European clubs. Those young playersâ¦ [combined with] star playersâ¦ a star in every way, with their lifestyle, their professionalism, their smile, their positive energy.

"Mohamed Salah is a really great example in this respect."

Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king? Published 5 days ago

Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king?

Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor? Published 6 August

Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor?

Attention 'cannot be given financial value'

During the off-season, Trabzonspor sold 20-year-old Ivorian midfielder Christ Inao Oulai to Fiorentina and Brazilian forward Felipe Augusto, 22, to Zenit St Petersburg - both for large profits after only one season at the club.

Young players from Albania, Belgium, Cape Verde and Portugal have arrived to replace them, but Dogan wants to continue balancing those talents with experienced names.

Cameroon goalkeeper Andre Onana has returned for a second season on loan from Manchester United, but the deal for Salah is the potential gamechanger.

"The attention it has generated and the level of engagement it has created around the world cannot easily be given a direct financial value," explained Dogan, who has openly admitted that Salah will be earning â¬17m per year (Â£14.6m, $19.9m), as well as 20% of any merchandise with his name on.

"Purely from a financial perspective, this transfer has no direct return as such.

"We put up our season tickets this year. We had to make another increase. I told our fans, 'Look, I'm bringing you Salah, one of the biggest stars in the world'."

Dogan says nearly 70% of Salah's salary this year was covered by season ticket sales made within the first four or five days after the announcement of his arrival.

The initial target was 25,000 season ticket sales, but the club now expects to exceed 30,000, while major companies have been calling the president, looking to get involved in Salah-mania.

"We're having important discussions in Turkey, Europe and the Arab world as well."

The news that Trabzonspor had won the race for Salah's signature after nine stellar seasons at Liverpool raised a few eyebrows.

Many had expected the man who sits fourth on the all-time list of Premier League goalscorers to sign a huge contract with a club in the Saudi Pro League like Cristiano Ronaldo or join Lionel Messi in the United States.

But while there was competition, Dogan says the deal happened quickly once negotiations really got going.

"Once we started talking, both sides genuinely approached each other very sincerely," he said.

"We'd actually been pursuing him since the World Cup, but we knew at the start he was also talking to other clubs."

This meant Trabzonspor initially had to bide their time, given Dogan says there is an unwritten rule in Turkey that if one club is holding talks then the others will wait.

"Yes, there were clubs in Turkey who were interested," he confirmed.

"After they said, 'We've pulled out of this transfer', we started talks. I think it took about five or six days to conclude.

"We had the first meeting over Zoom. At that point it was really just the two sides getting to know each other. Then Salah was on holiday - he was in Mykonos - and after that the talks continued again via Zoom."

Trabzonspor finally brought Salah to Turkey for his medical in Istanbul.

Dogan says they decided to hold it there to show the 34-year-old the kind of reception he would get across Turkey, not just in Trabzon.

Thousands of fans were at the airport to greet Salah when he arrived, even though it was in the middle of a working day.

Trabzonspor's new star also made his debut in Istanbul, entering the fray as a second-half substitute in a 1-1 draw against Kasimpasa on the opening day of the new league season last weekend.

He is expected to make his home league debut in Trabzon on Sunday.

"The whole city lives for football," said Dogan.

"Everywhere you go, on every corner, the city gives that player that energy and that happiness."

Thanks to Mohamed Salah, Trabzonspor's president could be smiling for a while yet.

Located on the Black Sea coast, the city of Trabzon sits near the border with Georgia in the north-east corner of Turkey.
With a population of around 800,000 people, it is not even in the top 20 when it comes to the country's largest urban centres.
But Dogan claims it has something special.
"I always say this about Trabzonspor and the city - we're the biggest one-club city in the world.
"Salah asked us something like, 'Why should I choose Trabzonspor now?'
"We told him about the city and said: 'You can be sure you will meet a group of supporters unlike any you have experienced before. You'll feel the genuine love those people have inside them'."
Born in January 1977, Dogan is himself a son of Trabzon.
The businessman made his money through a series of different ventures, including real estate and hazelnuts, before moving into the energy sector and specialising in biofuels.
He became Trabzonspor president in 2023, shortly after the club's most successful season in recent memory - having won the league title in 2021-22.
Under Dogan's watch, the Black Sea Storm, as the club is known, have finished third, seventh and third in the Super Lig.

Last season they won the Turkish Cup under coach Fatih Tekke, who is now looking to guide his team into the Europa League, despite a 1-0 home defeat in the first leg of their play-off tie against Hungary's Ferencvaros.
"We are working to make Trabzonspor and Trabzon itself a destination for talented young players from all over the world," said Dogan.

"We want to take them to the next level, to move on to bigger European clubs. Those young playersâ¦ [combined with] star playersâ¦ a star in every way, with their lifestyle, their professionalism, their smile, their positive energy.
"Mohamed Salah is a really great example in this respect."
Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king? Published 5 days ago
Who replaces Salah as Africa's Premier League king?
Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor? Published 6 August
Why has Salah chosen to join Trabzonspor?
Attention 'cannot be given financial value'

During the off-season, Trabzonspor sold 20-year-old Ivorian midfielder Christ Inao Oulai to Fiorentina and Brazilian forward Felipe Augusto, 22, to Zenit St Petersburg - both for large profits after only one season at the club.
Young players from Albania, Belgium, Cape Verde and Portugal have arrived to replace them, but Dogan wants to continue balancing those talents with experienced names.
Cameroon goalkeeper Andre Onana has returned for a second season on loan from Manchester United, but the deal for Salah is the potential gamechanger.

"The attention it has generated and the level of engagement it has created around the world cannot easily be given a direct financial value," explained Dogan, who has openly admitted that Salah will be earning â¬17m per year (Â£14.6m, $19.9m), as well as 20% of any merchandise with his name on.
"Purely from a financial perspective, this transfer has no direct return as such.
"We put up our season tickets this year. We had to make another increase. I told our fans, 'Look, I'm bringing you Salah, one of the biggest stars in the world'."
Dogan says nearly 70% of Salah's salary this year was covered by season ticket sales made within the first four or five days after the announcement of his arrival.
The initial target was 25,000 season ticket sales, but the club now expects to exceed 30,000, while major companies have been calling the president, looking to get involved in Salah-mania.
"We're having important discussions in Turkey, Europe and the Arab world as well."
The news that Trabzonspor had won the race for Salah's signature after nine stellar seasons at Liverpool raised a few eyebrows.

Many had expected the man who sits fourth on the all-time list of Premier League goalscorers to sign a huge contract with a club in the Saudi Pro League like Cristiano Ronaldo or join Lionel Messi in the United States.
But while there was competition, Dogan says the deal happened quickly once negotiations really got going.
"Once we started talking, both sides genuinely approached each other very sincerely," he said.
"We'd actually been pursuing him since the World Cup, but we knew at the start he was also talking to other clubs."
This meant Trabzonspor initially had to bide their time, given Dogan says there is an unwritten rule in Turkey that if one club is holding talks then the others will wait.
"Yes, there were clubs in Turkey who were interested," he confirmed.
"After they said, 'We've pulled out of this transfer', we started talks. I think it took about five or six days to conclude.

"We had the first meeting over Zoom. At that point it was really just the two sides getting to know each other. Then Salah was on holiday - he was in Mykonos - and after that the talks continued again via Zoom."
Trabzonspor finally brought Salah to Turkey for his medical in Istanbul.
Dogan says they decided to hold it there to show the 34-year-old the kind of reception he would get across Turkey, not just in Trabzon.
Thousands of fans were at the airport to greet Salah when he arrived, even though it was in the middle of a working day.
Trabzonspor's new star also made his debut in Istanbul, entering the fray as a second-half substitute in a 1-1 draw against Kasimpasa on the opening day of the new league season last weekend.
He is expected to make his home league debut in Trabzon on Sunday.
"The whole city lives for football," said Dogan.
"Everywhere you go, on every corner, the city gives that player that energy and that happiness."
Thanks to Mohamed Salah, Trabzonspor's president could be smiling for a while yet.

articles.title: FIFA Announces Bans, Fines Stemming from Argentina's Fight with Spain After World Cup Final
articles.summary: FIFA announced Friday that multiple players and a coach from the Argentina men's national team, plus a player from Spain's national team have been punished for their role in a post-match brawl following Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final on July 19.
articles.body:
FIFA announced Friday that multiple players and a coach from the Argentina men's national team, plus a player from Spain's national team have been punished for their role in a post-match brawl following Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the World Cup final on July 19.

FIFA fined and levied a 10-match ban against Leandro Paredes, a seven-match ban against Nahuel Molina a one-match ban against Thiago Almada and a three-match ban against assistant coach Roberto Ayala, all of whom represent Argentina. Spain's Pablo Martín Gavira (Gavi) received a one-match ban as well:

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

Per Ben Jacobs of GiveMeSport, the Argentinian Football Association was fined $321,000, and Argentina's next two home matches in international play will see their spectator capacity limited to 50 percent:

Multiple members of the Argentine and Spanish national teams clashed after the final whistle blew for the World Cup final, including Paredes knocking both Gavi and Eric Garcia to the ground:

Tempers seemingly flared for Argentina following a disappointing performance in their attempt to become the first nation to win back-to-back World Cups since Brazil in 1958 and 1962.

Paredes, 32, was part of Argentina's World Cup-winning squad in 2022, and he currently plays his club soccer for Boca Juniors in Argentina.

Molina and Almada also won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022, and they play their club soccer for AS Roma and River Plate, respectively.

Ayala, 53, earned 116 caps for the Argentine senior national team as a center-back before transitioning into coaching and joining Argentina's staff in 2019.

Gavi, who was the only Spanish player to receive a punishment, is a 22-year-old midfielder for FC Barcelona.

In addition to winning his first World Cup title with Spain this year, Gavi is a three-time La Liga champion with Barca.

articles.title: Usain Bolt: Olympics icon registers to play for Manchester Sunday league team
articles.summary: Eight-time Olympic champion sprinter Usain Bolt has registered to play for a veterans' Sunday league football team in Manchester.
articles.body:
Eight-time Olympic champion sprinter Usain Bolt has registered to play for a veterans' Sunday league football team in Manchester.

The Football Association's Full-Time website has the 40-year-old Jamaican as a registered player for Wythenshawe Vets FC, who play in the Premier Division of the Cheshire Veterans Football League.

The over-35s team based in south Manchester attracted attention last year for assembling a squad full of former Premier League players .

Wythenshawe's squad for this season includes former professionals such as England and Liverpool striker Emile Heskey, Everton striker Oumar Niasse, Manchester United captain Antonio Valencia, Newcastle striker Papiss Cisse, Manchester City duo Stephen Ireland and Nedum Onuoha and Premier League title winners Joleon Lescott and Danny Drinkwater.

Bolt is the fastest man in history over 100m and 200m, having set the world records for both distances at the 2009 Athletics World Championships.

After retiring from athletics in 2017, he pursued a career in professional football.

In 2018 Bolt scored twice in a friendly for Australian A-League side Central Coast Mariners, and signed a contract with the club after rejecting a two-year offer from Maltese side Valletta, but left just eight weeks later.

Wythenshawe, who have not officially announced Bolt's registration, have been contacted for comment.

articles.title: Arsenal transfer news: Al-Hilal in advanced talks to sign Gabriel Martinelli
articles.summary: Arsenal are in advanced talks with Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal over the sale of Gabriel Martinelli for at least Â£50m.
articles.body:
Arsenal are in advanced talks with Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal over the sale of Gabriel Martinelli for at least Â£50m.

The Brazil international, 25, is free to leave the club this summer, with manager Mikel Arteta making it clear the attacker is not in his plans.

Discussions between the clubs have intensified in the last 24 hours, with a deal now close.

If a final agreement is reached, it will be up to Martinelli - who has already turned down a move to Galatasaray - to decide whether he wants to play in the Saudi Pro League.

The wage package Al-Hilal are offering is also understood to be significantly more than his reported Â£180,000-per-week deal at Arsenal .

Martinelli, who joined Arsenal from Brazilian side Ituano in 2019, has 12 months remaining on his deal at Emirates Stadium.

He made 53 appearances in all competitions last season, scoring 11 goals, as the Gunners won the Premier League title.

But he was left out of the squad for their league opener against Coventry on Friday, which the Gunners won 3-0.

Former Arsenal striker Ian Wright was critical of Arteta's decision to omit Martinelli from the squad, as well as the club's treatment of the forward.

"The way Martinelli is being treated at the moment, it really makes me feel uncomfortable," Wright told Sky Sports.

"I know they might want him out, and a lot of people might say, 'yeah, it's time for him to move him on'. But there's ways of doing that and it should suit him as well, how he wants to leave."

BBC Sport understands Arteta has made his position clear to Martinelli and explained his reasons why he has been left out of the squad.

Al-Hilal's interest in Martinelli runs alongside a move for Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins.

The England international did not feature in Aston Villa's opening weekend defeat by Brighton on Sunday, with manager Unai Emery refusing to guarantee the forward would stay at Villa Park.

articles.title: Premier League title race: Liverpool and Man City nowhere near Arsenal's level, says Gary Neville
articles.summary: Gary Neville predicts Manchester City and Liverpool will not challenge Arsenal this season for the Premier League title; Neville set to join Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football for Fulham vs Chelsea where the pair will reveal their season predictions with David Jones
articles.body:
Liverpool and Manchester City are well below the level required to win the Premier League title this season, says Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville.

City are entering the unknown after Pep Guardiola's departure, while Liverpool are rebuilding under Andoni Iraola.

A last-gasp Josko Gvardiol winner handed Enzo Maresca a 2-1 win in his first Premier League game in charge of City against Bournemouth and Liverpool also left it late to draw 2-2 with Newcastle.

Arsenal's opening win was far more straightforward, swatting aside Coventry City 3-0 with minimal fuss. With only one week gone, the Gunners are already odds-on with bookmakers to win the Premier League despite there being 37 games to go.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Latest on YOUR PL club!
  • Premier League fixtures & scores | FREE PL highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream Premier League games with no contract 📺

And Neville is struggling to see a situation where City or Liverpool challenge Arsenal this season.

Speaking on The Gary Neville Podcast, he said: "Last week when we were previewing the season, all I kept thinking about was that this is going to be the most unpredictable season. It's going to be intriguing because you've got new managers, you've got lots of new players, you've got so much change at the top.

"Arsenal should win this league by a street - and I don't sit here on Sunday evening thinking anything differently, we've seen Tottenham get beat, we've seen Manchester United get beat, we've seen Liverpool nearly get beat, we've seen City scrambling for a win at home, so everything we thought we would see, we're seeing. The unpredictable nature of teams at the top, probably not being good enough to go and basically do what they did last season and the season before and getting beat by teams that are well organised like Brentford and Hull and others.

"Man City are the same as Liverpool, these two clubs were getting nearly 100 points, six, seven years ago. Treble winners, four times Premier League winners, Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool, Arne Slot's champions, that's just happened and so we're measuring these two clubs by the standards that they've set, but they're nowhere near that standard.

"This Liverpool team are nowhere near the levels of a Premier League title winning team - they need a lot of work.

"I think they'll be happy with the point [vs Newcastle], a good finish for them, and they're celebrating, but I think deep down when you're measuring yourself and the standards that Liverpool have in the last five, 10 years of winning titles, I think they'll travel home, back to Liverpool and back to Merseyside, and they'll be thinking, we've got a lot of work to do.

"And Man City, they're well below where they need to be. Losing Rodri is a massive blow."

Nev 'so sure' Arsenal will win Premier League

With City and Liverpool lagging behind, Neville can see a situation where Chelsea could be Arsenal's closest rivals in the title race.

Xabi Alonso's men get their campaign off and running on Monday Night Football at Fulham, where Neville will be joining Jamie Carragher to reveal his season predictions.

Neville added: "Arsenal are going to be feeling really confident right now.

"It's the most sure I've ever been, and look it could be that I've got egg on my face at the end of the season, [but] it's the most sure I've ever been after game one that we're going to see a team be Premier League champions.

"Chelsea will finish second, unless I see them play really badly at Fulham, so I do reserve the right to change my opinion. I do think Chelsea will finish second because of the squad and because of the fact they haven't got European competition.

"They haven't got the confusion, they've got a good manager, so I do think Chelsea have got a great chance to push Arsenal this year and finish second and be the team and let's see on Monday night."

articles.title: What does your Scottish Premiership club need in final 11 days of transfer window?
articles.summary: BBC Scotland assesses the 12 top-flight clubs' needs as the transfer deadline approaches.
articles.body:
Just 11 days remain for managers in the Scottish Premiership to do their final bit of wheeling and dealing before January.

It's a well-known observation that managers hate doing business in the winter window, with most signings either a stop-gap solution or a desperate bid to turn things around.

So what must the current crop of Premiership bosses do to avoid such signings in the future?

Where are the glaring gaps in the squad? Who needs to cut adrift some deadwood? And who needs to keep their star player up under lock and key?

With 13 players already through the entrance and 14 through the exit, it's been a busy old summer at Pittodrie.

Seemingly, head coach Stephen Robinson has opted to start from scratch when moulding his new squad but there's still a few blank spots on an increasingly busy picture.

While fans may be keen for some energy in midfield and perhaps another winger, Robinson has stated publicly that he still has too many players at his disposal.

With a squad size of 28, the third biggest in the league, it is more likely the head coach will be flaunting his wares at the market, rather than adding to his squad.

While Martin O'Neill's starting XI looks fairly settled thanks to Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran hitting the ground running, the bench at Celtic Park still looks fairly sparse.

That won't be helped by the expected exit of midfielder Reo Hatate and the injury to right-back Alistair Johnston who, according to reports, is facing an extended spell on the sidelines.

After the Â£22m fee received for Arne Engels, there might be more money to strengthen the back-up brigade.

Viljami Sinisalo could do with some more competition in the sticks and, while youngster Colby Donovan has impressed so far, perhaps another right-back is needed for the Champions League.

Most important is finding a suitable back-up for Kieran Tierney. O'Neill has previously stated that the 29-year-old's minutes need managed but he is the only senior left-back on the books.

With just 22 first-team players at his disposal - and one of them now injured for the season in Simon Murray - Steven Pressley has the smallest squad in the league.

He has just five defenders, plus Drey Wright, who could probably play across the back-four if needed. Out wide, the numbers are also limited.

Pressley has been at pains to point out the fact that Yan Dhanda and Cam Congreve - two of their best players last season - didn't sign until late in the window.

They've made a good start, but they need reinforcements in at least two areas. Will Pressley be able to replicate his success in the loan market?

Ferry to depart and leave gap for Dundee United?

Jim Goodwin has already brought 12 players into Tannadice this summer, in a window that seemed to suggest a change of approach.

The noise from Tayside was Goodwin wanted a more homegrown approach to implement an attractive, ball-on-the-floor, style of play.

If the signature of Dylan Tait hinted at this move, the addition of Abdoulaye Yoro and Idjessi Metsoko flew in the face of it. It's hard to know what comes next.

The main issue will be finding a replacement for Will Ferry, the former United vice-captain and stand-out left-back who has excelled in recent seasons. The Irishman, who made his international debut in May, is widely expected to depart for a sizeable fee.

Romanian international Kevin Ciubotaru has arrived but he would be the only left-back in the squad should Ferry depart.

There is also an issue up front, given the current record of one goal from the past four games. Whether Lachlan Rose or Zac Sapsford can play up top by themselves remains up for debate, while Metsoko - like Ciubotaru - is still an unknown quantity

No-one has signed more players so far than Falkirk, with 14 arrivals under the watchful eye of John McGlynn.

The Bairns boss, like Pressley, worked his magic in the loan window last season with the additions of defender Filip Lissah, attacking midfielder Ben Broggio and wingers Kyrell Wilson and Ethan Williams.

They've all returned home, or since moved on, and McGlynn must replace them and the goals of Barney Stewart and Calvin Miller.

After the signing of midfielder Finley Barbrook on loan from Ipswich, the manager said there might be as many as three more additions. So far, he's only gotten striker Jacob Morrell from DC United through the door.

It's hard to see where the other two would fit without the squad becoming bloated.

What does future hold for Hearts' Braga?

The biggest squad in the league and, if rumours are to be believed, they're not done yet. American striker JJ Williams is seemingly in Edinburgh, all 6'4" of him, before a proposed medical and move.

He would add to the goalscoring threats of Pierre Landry Kabore, Amadou Ba-Sy, James Wilson and Elton Kabangu - albeit the latter of those is waiting in the departure lounge.

Wouter Vrancken has discussed his desire to trim the squad to an ideal size of 27 players, but it currently sits at 32.

Who else could go? Attacking midfielders Yan Dhanda and Sander Kartum are at the top of that list.

Then there's Claudio Braga. Linked with a big-money move away all summer, the Portuguese has been strong in his message that he will give his all until the second he leaves.

If he were to go, Hearts certainly have the numbers. It remains to be seen whether they have the same quality.

Unlike every other club in the league, other than maybe Celtic, it's been a quiet summer in Leith.

Six signings, only two permanent departures in Chris Cadden and Elie Youan. David Gray has opted for the consistent approach but has said he thinks they are thin on the ground in some areas.

Similar to Hearts and Dundee United, though, it might be more about keeping their big star - or replacing him quickly if he does go. That big star is, of course, Josh Mulligan.

He is the latest young Scot to be linked with a move to Serie A and, given the exploits of former Hibees Kieron Bowie and Josh Doig at Sassuolo, he might be tempted to join them.

Neil McCann's recruitment was rightly lauded in January after his signings transformed the squad and helped keep Killie up.

It's not gone quite as well in this window. None of his signings have made a big impact in either the League Cup or the Premiership and the defence is leaking goals.

Despite that, centre-back George Stanger has been linked with a move to Burton Albion. Another defender is a must, with some fans keen on a return for former Killie man Joe Wright.

Further reinforcements are needed on the right, with Jamie Brandon the only recognised right-back and the attacking flank on that side also looking sparse.

Should Motherwell cash in on Maswanhise?

With nine summer signings, Alfred Johannson seems to be quite settled on his current squad - even if there are rumours of a new winger on the way.

There are already plenty of numbers at the top end of the pitch but a number of them are out injured.

Having already sold Elijah Just, Elliot Watt and Calum Ward for big money, they might be loathe to lose Tawanda Maswanhise, but the Zimbabwean only has two goals in his past 17 games.

His contract expires next summer with Motherwell holding an option to extend it by a further 12 months. Is now the time to cash in?

Of all the Premiership supporters who have been unhappy with their side's start, Rangers are right up there.

Last season's leadership has almost entirely been cleared out - John Souttar is expected to depart - but a void has been left.

Emmanuel Fernandez continues to draw interest, despite a poor start to the season, and supporters seem desperate for a new centre-back.

The 11 new signings have yet to bed in, Ben Godfrey has already picked up an injury, and former Hearts men Cammy Devlin and Lawrence Shankland - made club captain in his first few weeks - have found themselves on the bench.

The squad is also full of players who seem to no longer be, or never were, part of Derek McInnes' plans. Young Scots Connor Barron and Lyall Cameron have reportedly been told to find new clubs, Clinton Nsiala and Jose Cifuentes have not been spotted under the new manager, while Ross McCausland and Bojan Miovski seem unfancied.

With Youssef Chermiti out for the season, McInnes may also have to dip into the market to find another striker.

Simo Valakari is waiting on Fifa ratifying his move for Bosnian left-back Enes Alic, with his homeland club FK ZeljezniÂ­car claiming he is still their player.

That is a move that is desperately needed, with Matthew Foulds currently the only available left-back, leaving Liam Smith having to cover.

While that transfer saga rumbles on, another right-back option and central midfielder could be on the Finn's shopping list. While Reece McAlear, Jason Holt, Sam Stanton and Macaulay Tait are all decent options, they might need a little more pedigree.

Former Mansfield Town midfielder Aaron Lewis was being looked at, but the Perth Saints decided against offering him a contract.

Keeping hold of Killian Phillips will be Craig McLeish's biggest challenge in the next 11 days. The American-born midfielder has been attracting interest from the MLS for the past eight months, with their window shutting a day before Scotland's.

With Calvin Ramsay's arrival at right-back seemingly imminent, it is another striker that most fans want.

Mikael Mandron, Jonah Ayunga, Dan Nlundulu and Kion Etete were strikers in the squad last season. They've all moved on, or are unavailable, with only Eseosa Sule and Jake Young to replace them.

At the back, Alex Gogic and Marcus Fraser have been the starting centre-backs with Richard King well down the pecking order. After the departure of Miguel Freckleton, another centre-back wouldn't go amiss.
paragraphs: Just 11 days remain for managers in the Scottish Premiership to do their final bit of wheeling and dealing before January.
It's a well-known observation that managers hate doing business in the winter window, with most signings either a stop-gap solution or a desperate bid to turn things around.
So what must the current crop of Premiership bosses do to avoid such signings in the future?
Where are the glaring gaps in the squad? Who needs to cut adrift some deadwood? And who needs to keep their star player up under lock and key?
With 13 players already through the entrance and 14 through the exit, it's been a busy old summer at Pittodrie.
Seemingly, head coach Stephen Robinson has opted to start from scratch when moulding his new squad but there's still a few blank spots on an increasingly busy picture.
While fans may be keen for some energy in midfield and perhaps another winger, Robinson has stated publicly that he still has too many players at his disposal.
With a squad size of 28, the third biggest in the league, it is more likely the head coach will be flaunting his wares at the market, rather than adding to his squad.
While Martin O'Neill's starting XI looks fairly settled thanks to Kasper Hogh and Camilo Duran hitting the ground running, the bench at Celtic Park still looks fairly sparse.
That won't be helped by the expected exit of midfielder Reo Hatate and the injury to right-back Alistair Johnston who, according to reports, is facing an extended spell on the sidelines.
After the Â£22m fee received for Arne Engels, there might be more money to strengthen the back-up brigade.
Viljami Sinisalo could do with some more competition in the sticks and, while youngster Colby Donovan has impressed so far, perhaps another right-back is needed for the Champions League.
Most important is finding a suitable back-up for Kieran Tierney. O'Neill has previously stated that the 29-year-old's minutes need managed but he is the only senior left-back on the books.
With just 22 first-team players at his disposal - and one of them now injured for the season in Simon Murray - Steven Pressley has the smallest squad in the league.
He has just five defenders, plus Drey Wright, who could probably play across the back-four if needed. Out wide, the numbers are also limited.
Pressley has been at pains to point out the fact that Yan Dhanda and Cam Congreve - two of their best players last season - didn't sign until late in the window.
They've made a good start, but they need reinforcements in at least two areas. Will Pressley be able to replicate his success in the loan market?
Ferry to depart and leave gap for Dundee United?
Jim Goodwin has already brought 12 players into Tannadice this summer, in a window that seemed to suggest a change of approach.
The noise from Tayside was Goodwin wanted a more homegrown approach to implement an attractive, ball-on-the-floor, style of play.
If the signature of Dylan Tait hinted at this move, the addition of Abdoulaye Yoro and Idjessi Metsoko flew in the face of it. It's hard to know what comes next.

The main issue will be finding a replacement for Will Ferry, the former United vice-captain and stand-out left-back who has excelled in recent seasons. The Irishman, who made his international debut in May, is widely expected to depart for a sizeable fee.
Romanian international Kevin Ciubotaru has arrived but he would be the only left-back in the squad should Ferry depart.

There is also an issue up front, given the current record of one goal from the past four games. Whether Lachlan Rose or Zac Sapsford can play up top by themselves remains up for debate, while Metsoko - like Ciubotaru - is still an unknown quantity
No-one has signed more players so far than Falkirk, with 14 arrivals under the watchful eye of John McGlynn.

The Bairns boss, like Pressley, worked his magic in the loan window last season with the additions of defender Filip Lissah, attacking midfielder Ben Broggio and wingers Kyrell Wilson and Ethan Williams.
They've all returned home, or since moved on, and McGlynn must replace them and the goals of Barney Stewart and Calvin Miller.

After the signing of midfielder Finley Barbrook on loan from Ipswich, the manager said there might be as many as three more additions. So far, he's only gotten striker Jacob Morrell from DC United through the door.
It's hard to see where the other two would fit without the squad becoming bloated.

The biggest squad in the league and, if rumours are to be believed, they're not done yet. American striker JJ Williams is seemingly in Edinburgh, all 6'4" of him, before a proposed medical and move.
He would add to the goalscoring threats of Pierre Landry Kabore, Amadou Ba-Sy, James Wilson and Elton Kabangu - albeit the latter of those is waiting in the departure lounge.

articles.title: Ranking the 10 Worst Kits in World Football for the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The new season is finally here. Club football is back mere minutes after the 2026 FIFA World Cup finished, bringing with it a new set of awful kits to digest.
articles.body:
The new season is finally here. Club football is back mere minutes after the 2026 FIFA World Cup finished, bringing with it a new set of awful kits to digest.

If you like bad colourways, questionable designs and big clubs just getting it wrong, this is for you.

The shirt is actually quite nice from far away, but get closer and the neon stripes start to look a lot more like claw marks. It has training-top energy, something bold enough to get people interested, but really should only be worn before matches.

The thing is, Spurs' purple third shirt would make quite a nice away kit. It's not great by any means, but it does seem more fitting than this Nike concoction, which looks weirder the longer you stare at it. What's that line above the sponsor?

To be fair to FC Basel, they might have the two worst kits combined this year.

The home shirt's red and blue are so bold, it's like when you accidentally set hue and saturation to extremes when editing kits on the old Pro Evolution Soccer games.

The away kit goes the other way, appearing as if it's lost all sense of personality after a heavy wash. Yellow and white are a very flushed-out colour combination. So much so, you can't even really see the club badge.

Do you remember those optical illusions that force you to stare at an unbearable pattern in the hope an image pops out? Norwich City's third shirt is like that, but what appears is just short of a headache.

The purple-and-mint design looks just like the seats on old English buses. The Canaries launched the shirt with photos on a bus, so it's probably what they were going for…

Maybe more kits need to lean into old niches like that. Next season could be based on the parachute game or hopscotch.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

A good example of getting too creative for the sake of it.

Real Madrid's home shirt doesn't need green and red stripes; the latter are completely distracting. It's rare for Adidas to miss the mark for one of its big clubs, but this just isn't cutting it, as it doesn't come across as classic or particularly modern.

Instead, Los Blancos' new home kit looks like one your mate would pick up cheap in bulk ahead of your next five-a-side match against Dungdee United.

South African side Kaizer Chiefs have had some bangers over the years. They pretty much always try to do something different. That should be applauded.

This year's away kit silences those claps.

The spiky design is meant to mirror a lion's mane, but the way the sponsor sits on it is uneven. The top looks like a sports bra, and the bottom is so bare that it brings attention to the Charlie Brown vibe that dominates everything. Not good.

I have a theory that FC Luzern decided to put out an ugly away kit so their special anniversary shirt would look even better. The latter is beautiful—a classic design that could be worn away from the football pitch.

The away kit, though, is struggling under the pressure of that thick blue stripe with a smaller gold stripe inside.

There's interesting history behind the idea, which takes inspiration from the Jesuit church, but it's a heavy-handed design that isn't helped by the stripe and neckline combo looking like a Lego hand pointing upwards.

There's an air of Only Fools & Horses about the chevron design on a shirt that is doing way too much.

Maybe it'd look good with a flat cap, down the betting shop. Maybe multiple blues on multiple reds, with a stripe on the collar and sleeves, stamped with a less-than-elegant sponsor isn't going to create the nicest shirt in the world.

To stick with the old British comedy analogies…Bournemouth's home shirt is reminiscent of Kryten from Red Dwarf .

That middle circle, with the encased sponsor, looks like the perfect hole to slot in a hoover or whisk.

If you have no idea what I'm talking about, do yourself a favour and seek the show out. I promise it's funnier than this article.

Adidas' brief for Newcastle's new shirt must have been: "Take the classic black and white stripes and absolutely batter them." We've got wide, we've got narrow. There's so much going on when, similar to iconic strips like Ajax, it just needs to be toned down.

To make things worse, the Magpies' rivals will be wearing one of the nicest home shirts of the season. Sunderland went ultra classic with it, rather than working to destroy an easy seller each year by dressing the team up as human barcodes.

Austrian side TSV Hartberg collect sponsors like an old rocker collects stitched badges for their denim jacket.

Their kits are defined by commercial spew. All of the shirts are basic, aside from being packed with seemingly any company who will give the club money.

There can't be a world where fans will look at these and say, "Oh yeah, I'm spending money on that." But then, perhaps that's the point. The money could already be locked in, with the knowledge that any shirt featuring "Spermbooster" probably has its own special place in football history.

articles.title: Expert College Football Betting Locks for 2026 Win Total Bets
articles.summary: On paper, it all looks so easy.
articles.body:
The wins and losses seem so clear months in advance, before a single point is scored in the college football season. The reality, however, is that the unexpected will become the norm, and many of the assumptions made in August will prove wrong, one way or another.

Which brings us to the task of tackling this year's lineup of win totals. Perhaps no future bet is more direct than this one, the art of predicting whether a football team will overperform or underperform.

Some games are locks. Some are coin flips. Some, for most, are uphill climbs. Very little of it will go to plan, although a final number will be decided at the end.

With no shortage of teams to pick from, that's what we set out to do today. From the good to the (potentially) bad, here are some of the win totals we like heading into the season.

With so much change, there is much to discuss. But rather than start at the QB or the coach or the many new faces, we must start with the schedule.

In fact, let's take it a step further: Double woof.

Penn State does not play Ohio State, Indiana or Oregon. Road games at Michigan and Washington will be a challenge, and a home game against USC won't be easy. But Matt Campbell is primed to start his Happy Valley tenure with a bang.

As for the roster, it features a plethora of new faces. The most important is unquestionably quarterback Rocco Becht, who joined Campbell at Penn State along with his offensive coordinator.

Also joining them is tight end Benjamin Brahmer, who was a massive, critical weapon for Becht in Ames.

The defense should be solid immediately thanks to defensive coordinator D'Anton Lynn, who worked wonders at USC. He'll have to manage a defense filled with change, and he'll have capable players to work with.

Everything is aligned here for Penn State to win 10 games, even if that might seem a little too soon for some.

The good news for those who feel South Carolina is capable of a bounceback season is that things start favorably.

Kent State, Towson and Mississippi State are on the docket to start the year, although the game against the Bulldogs is no pushover. From there, perhaps outside of a road trip to Arkansas, the schedule is an absolute gauntlet.

Road trips include visits to Alabama, Florida, Oklahoma and Clemson. South Carolina will also play Tennessee, Texas A&M and Georgia.

Yes, there is talent on this roster. In fact, the high-end talent is exceptional. Dylan Stewart is an elite defensive player. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers and wideout Nyck Harbor have seemingly unlimited potential on offense.

Sellers, in particular, is critical. He must play better than he did last year, and he likely will be. But unless he takes that next step, it's hard to envision South Carolina navigating such a difficult path without anything beyond bowl eligibility.

No team underwent a more extensive makeover than Oklahoma State. Mike Gundy was fired, Eric Morris was hired and the roster was essentially remade from scratch.

The most interesting part, however, is what Morris brought with him to start. For all the new faces, none are more impactful than quarterback Drew Mestemaker and running back Caleb Hawkins.

Both give this team a shot. It's that simple.

Sure, the pieces have to come together in a short period of time, but such is life in college football in 2026.

For a team with so many new parts, the schedule (and conference) cooperates. A Week 2 game against Oregon likely won't go well. But beyond that, no individual game on the schedule feels unconquerable.

One of the few certainties in the Big 12 is that Texas Tech, even with questions at QB, appears to be the most talented team in the conference by a wide margin. Outside of that, the path is clear for a team like Oklahoma State to break through.

It's a lot to ask for a program that has changed so much. But the talent at key positions gives them a shot.

The roster is talented, the head coach is excellent, and the team is coming off a College Football Playoff showing. With that firmly acknowledged, the Aggies could struggle to deliver the kind of season they did one season ago.

On offense, the line had to be remade and KC Concepcion, the team's best wideout, is off to the NFL.

Marcel Reed certainly has plenty of skills, but his accuracy remains a work in progress. It was also evident in his team's final two games last season. Against Texas and Miami, the QB accounted for four interceptions and no scores.

Again, he can be great. But it's fair to assess just how much better he will be, especially with many new pieces around him.

The other reality A&M faces is the schedule. Last year, things broke well. The Aggies were 4-0 in the regular season in games decided by a touchdown or less, and they certainly needed plenty of unique moments to get there.

This year, things seem tougher on paper. It doesn't start terribly tough, although the final five games are as such: at Alabama, at South Carolina, vs. Tennessee, at Oklahoma and vs. Texas.

When you retrace how exactly Ole Miss came within a few plays of making the national championship, it still doesn't feel quite real.

The Rebels changed their starting QB, lost their coach and somehow kept it together amid chaos. Now, Pete Golding will have a shot at delivering an encore from start to finish.

In many respects, this is a bet on Trinidad Chambliss. He started the year as an unknown backup, and he emerged as one of the most exciting players in all of college football. Having running back Kewan Lacy back gives Ole Miss the most electric tandem in the country.

Sure, the schedule is brutal. Of course it is.

The Rebels start with Louisville, and that won't be a picnic. They're currently a less-than-a-touchdown favorite.

They'll play LSU a few weeks later at home, which promises to be one of the wildest environments of the year. Games at Florida, Texas and Oklahoma will also be challenging.

Like many in the SEC, the schedule will require plenty of things to go right and key players to stay healthy. But the quarterback is simply sensational, and that alone is worth betting on.

Sure, the offseason was turbulent. Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. was seemingly headed elsewhere, although he landed back with his team from a year ago. Washington has a cozy start to its season and a slew of winnable games along the way. Anything less than eight wins would surprise.

The Cougars were a tremendous surprise last year, and head coach Willie Fritz will have quarterback Conner Weigman back. Still, the offensive line needs major massaging and the schedule, in particular the road trips on tap, could make this a more difficult campaign to navigate.

There's not a game on the schedule that doesn't feel like it can't be won. A road trip to Vanderbilt and a home game against Louisville are the highlights on paper, and even those games can be conquered. The rest of the slate is supremely manageable, and quarterback CJ Bailey is poised for a breakout year.

Pat Fitzgerald is back, and we'll see how exactly he fits Michigan State long term. In the short term, he's coming into a difficult situation. Having to play Notre Dame in an out-of-conference game is not what any first-year head coach wants. And while some of the conference games feel like a coin flip, Sparty might not be ready for what's about to transpire.
