Kent State, Towson and Mississippi State are on the docket to start the year, although the game against the Bulldogs is no pushover. From there, perhaps outside of a road trip to Arkansas, the schedule is an absolute gauntlet.
Road trips include visits to Alabama, Florida, Oklahoma and Clemson. South Carolina will also play Tennessee, Texas A&M and Georgia.

Yes, there is talent on this roster. In fact, the high-end talent is exceptional. Dylan Stewart is an elite defensive player. Quarterback LaNorris Sellers and wideout Nyck Harbor have seemingly unlimited potential on offense.

Sellers, in particular, is critical. He must play better than he did last year, and he likely will be. But unless he takes that next step, it's hard to envision South Carolina navigating such a difficult path without anything beyond bowl eligibility.
No team underwent a more extensive makeover than Oklahoma State. Mike Gundy was fired, Eric Morris was hired and the roster was essentially remade from scratch.
The most interesting part, however, is what Morris brought with him to start. For all the new faces, none are more impactful than quarterback Drew Mestemaker and running back Caleb Hawkins.
Both give this team a shot. It's that simple.
Sure, the pieces have to come together in a short period of time, but such is life in college football in 2026.

For a team with so many new parts, the schedule (and conference) cooperates. A Week 2 game against Oregon likely won't go well. But beyond that, no individual game on the schedule feels unconquerable.

One of the few certainties in the Big 12 is that Texas Tech, even with questions at QB, appears to be the most talented team in the conference by a wide margin. Outside of that, the path is clear for a team like Oklahoma State to break through.
It's a lot to ask for a program that has changed so much. But the talent at key positions gives them a shot.

The roster is talented, the head coach is excellent, and the team is coming off a College Football Playoff showing. With that firmly acknowledged, the Aggies could struggle to deliver the kind of season they did one season ago.
On offense, the line had to be remade and KC Concepcion, the team's best wideout, is off to the NFL.

Marcel Reed certainly has plenty of skills, but his accuracy remains a work in progress. It was also evident in his team's final two games last season. Against Texas and Miami, the QB accounted for four interceptions and no scores.
Again, he can be great. But it's fair to assess just how much better he will be, especially with many new pieces around him.

The other reality A&M faces is the schedule. Last year, things broke well. The Aggies were 4-0 in the regular season in games decided by a touchdown or less, and they certainly needed plenty of unique moments to get there.
This year, things seem tougher on paper. It doesn't start terribly tough, although the final five games are as such: at Alabama, at South Carolina, vs. Tennessee, at Oklahoma and vs. Texas.
When you retrace how exactly Ole Miss came within a few plays of making the national championship, it still doesn't feel quite real.
The Rebels changed their starting QB, lost their coach and somehow kept it together amid chaos. Now, Pete Golding will have a shot at delivering an encore from start to finish.

In many respects, this is a bet on Trinidad Chambliss. He started the year as an unknown backup, and he emerged as one of the most exciting players in all of college football. Having running back Kewan Lacy back gives Ole Miss the most electric tandem in the country.
Sure, the schedule is brutal. Of course it is.
The Rebels start with Louisville, and that won't be a picnic. They're currently a less-than-a-touchdown favorite.
They'll play LSU a few weeks later at home, which promises to be one of the wildest environments of the year. Games at Florida, Texas and Oklahoma will also be challenging.
Like many in the SEC, the schedule will require plenty of things to go right and key players to stay healthy. But the quarterback is simply sensational, and that alone is worth betting on.

Sure, the offseason was turbulent. Quarterback Demond Williams Jr. was seemingly headed elsewhere, although he landed back with his team from a year ago. Washington has a cozy start to its season and a slew of winnable games along the way. Anything less than eight wins would surprise.

The Cougars were a tremendous surprise last year, and head coach Willie Fritz will have quarterback Conner Weigman back. Still, the offensive line needs major massaging and the schedule, in particular the road trips on tap, could make this a more difficult campaign to navigate.

There's not a game on the schedule that doesn't feel like it can't be won. A road trip to Vanderbilt and a home game against Louisville are the highlights on paper, and even those games can be conquered. The rest of the slate is supremely manageable, and quarterback CJ Bailey is poised for a breakout year.

Pat Fitzgerald is back, and we'll see how exactly he fits Michigan State long term. In the short term, he's coming into a difficult situation. Having to play Notre Dame in an out-of-conference game is not what any first-year head coach wants. And while some of the conference games feel like a coin flip, Sparty might not be ready for what's about to transpire.

articles.title: James Morrison: West Bromwich Albion boss backs Aune Heggebo following deception ban
articles.summary: West Bromwich Albion head coach James Morrison says the FA have "opened a can of worms" over Aune Heggebo's two-match ban for deception.
articles.body:
West Bromwich Albion head coach James Morrison says the Football Association have "opened a can of worms" over Aune Heggebo's two-match ban for deception.

Jimmy-Jay Morgan's cross hit Heggebo's hand on its way into the net to give Albion the lead in their 2-1 win over Norwich City on the first day of the Championship season.

The Norway international forward last week became the first player to be charged with "deception of a match official" since the rule was introduced in the 2017-18 season.

Morrison said the incident was accidental and that the onus had not been on the player to tell referee Tim Robinson.

"We wanted to back Bo because he's not that type of person," he told BBC Radio WM.

"He was upset because he was saying it [the charge] was calling him a cheat, basically, and we all know he's not that.

"He'll be looking at the cross when it came in, it flicked from the goalkeeper's hands into him.

"He's not going to run to the referee is he, and say, 'I handballed that'? Not in a million years."

What does Heggebo's deception ban mean for football? Published 4 days ago

What does Heggebo's deception ban mean for football?

West Brom's Heggebo banned for 'handball goal' Published 5 days ago

West Brom's Heggebo banned for 'handball goal'

Controversial goal tees up West Brom win at Norwich

The "disappointed" Albion boss said the ban had opened "a can of worms for the FA" to punish what they deem as deception.

Heggebo, 25, missed Sunday's 3-1 win over Burnley in the Championship and will also miss the Carabao Cup tie away to Newcastle United on Wednesday (19:45 BST).

"If they're going to do it, we accept it, but they've got to be consistent throughout the season," Morrison added.

"Be consistent throughout the season and we can all deal with that."

articles.title: Derek McInnes: Rangers manager could be in stand for first Old Firm game after hearing date set
articles.summary: Derek McInnes could be in the stand for his first Old Firm match as Rangers manager after a hearing date of 31 August was set for his appeal against a touchline ban.
articles.body:
Derek McInnes could be in the stand for his first Old Firm match as Rangers manager after a hearing date of 31 August was set for his appeal against a four-match touchline ban, one game of which is suspended.

The penalty issued in July related to McInnes' spell as Hearts boss last season, when he described the decision to award Celtic a late penalty at Motherwell in May as "disgusting".

A stoppage-time spot-kick for handball was converted by Kelechi Iheanacho and Celtic's 3-2 victory at Fir Park on 13 May kept them one point behind Hearts, who they beat to the title a few days later in a final-day decider.

Rangers argued the remarks were "directed at the decision, rather than representing any broader criticism of officials" when announcing their intention to contest the ban.

And McInnes, who could be in the stand for games against Falkirk, Motherwell and Celtic, added: "I don't agree with it and the club don't agree with it. I'm glad that we're going to appeal against that.

"I've been a manager for 19 years and you know you're going to be asked about contentious decisions and all the rest of it.

"I've never wanted to make it personal. For me, the decision was wrong. I feel as though I made my points at the hearing.

"Broadcasters pay a lot of money to hear managers' reactions. We've got to be careful that we don't have managers and players who have to be really sure of themselves and check themselves before answering a question.

"At no point was I wanting to inflame a situation. The situation was already being discussed before I did my Press. It was quite a big moment in the season and there was a lot of emotion, but I felt as though what I said was controlled."

The games against Falkirk away on 2 September and Motherwell three days later at home immediately after the hearing are in the Scottish Premiership, while the 13 September visit of Celtic is in the quarter-finals of the League Cup.

Girona winger Kim to undergo Rangers medical Published 1 day ago

Girona winger Kim to undergo Rangers medical

Visit our Rangers page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

Speaking to Sky Sports after a win against Falkirk at Tynecastle on the same night as Celtic's win at Fir Park, McInnes said: "When you heard Celtic got a 96th-minute penalty that was going to VAR and they were checking it, you just assume what's happened is they get the penalty.

"Having seen it again, it's disgusting. It is. I don't think it's a penalty kick.

"But we're up against it. We're up against everybody."

Scottish FA head of referees Willie Collum later backed the call, citing "clear evidence" of Motherwell's Sam Nicholson's hand and arm "in an unnatural position" - and the resulting contact "a punishable handball".

Referee John Beaton's contact details were posted online, with police keeping his home under surveillance. A teenager was then charged "in connection with a data protection offence".

The statement from Rangers added: "Respect for officials and legitimate scrutiny are not competing principles.

"Managers, players and clubs must be able to speak honestly about major decisions if Scottish football is serious about raising standards and maintaining trust.

"Scrutiny, transparency and accountability should be seen as part of improving standards, not as a threat to them."

articles.title: College Fantasy Football: 26 stats Eric Froton finds relevant as we approach the 2026 season
articles.summary: Here are some key stats to note for the upcoming 2026 College Fantasy Football season.
articles.body:
The NFL fantasy realm is accustomed to preseason columns that highlight interesting statistics that might sway opinions on various players. With the 2026 College Fantasy Football season almost upon us, here are 26 stats that I find relevant when preparing for your upcoming Yahoo College Fantasy Football drafts.

Play Yahoo's new College Fantasy Football game: Create or join a league now!

1 - Of the top-10 scoring quarterbacks, six ran for 400+ yards, and all 10 ran for 200+ yards.

2 - Oregon TE Jamari Johnson ranked 37th overall among P4 tight ends with 45 targets in 2025. Despite splitting the TE workload with 2026 first-round pick Kenyon Sadiq, Johnson ranks No. 1 among all returning TEs with 16 Explosive (15+ yard) receptions.

3 - Despite being plagued by poor QB play at Michigan State, Indiana WR Nick Marsh racked up an astounding 28 missed tackles on just 58 receptions for a nation-leading 48.3% missed tackle rate.

4 - Texas A&M WR Ashton Bethel-Roman leads all returning wideouts with 40+ regular season targets with an average of 23.0 yards per catch and 4.2 fantasy points per touch. If he can improve upon his 46.5% catch rate, Bethel-Roman could be a viable sleeper.

5 - NC State-to-USC WR Terrell Anderson leads all returning 50+ target P4 wideouts with an ultra-efficient 12.5 yards per regular season target. He could very well wrest the WR1 role from Tanook Hines this year at USC, but is being drafted several rounds behind him.

6 - Texas-to-Oklahoma transfer Parker Livingstone quietly ranks 2nd among all 40+ target P4 WRs with 3.93 fantasy points per touch. He's also one of only 3 returning P4 receivers to throw a touchdown pass last year. Miami's Malachi Toney and NC State's Teddy Hoffman are the others.

7 - Raise the bar to 75 targets, and Colorado-to-Arizona State standout WR Omarion Miller leads all Power Four returnees with an average of 3.38 fantasy points per touch. He has a path to take over Jordyn Tyson's high-volume role at ASU, but has to compete with BC transfer Reed Harris for targets.

8 - Kentucky TE Willie Rodriguez paces all returning P4 tight ends who received 20+ targets with an 11.2-yard average depth of target. He flexed out on 63% of snaps and ranked third among Power Four returners in wide rate.

9 - Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy is the nation's top returning bell cow, leading the P4 with 256 regular season carries (306 total) and 23.0 fantasy points per game in 2025. Just three returning rushers averaged 20 fantasy PPG at the P4 level, the others being injured Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy and Rutgers RB Antwan Raymond.

10 - Speaking of Hardy, he averaged 6.4 yards per carry on 257 attempts last season…Jamal Roberts averaged 6.2 yards per carry on 123 attempts. Of the two, Roberts finished with a better breakaway percentage (Roberts: 50.1%, Hardy: 47.8%). Roberts was also the clear receiving back, out-targeting Hardy 24 to 7. Roberts is a lock-down every week starter until Hardy returns from his injury.

11 - Despite receiving just 26 touches last year, Notre Dame starting RB Aneyas Williams averaged a sensational 2.21 fantasy points per touch last year, which easily tops all returnees despite limited opportunity. For perspective, the two next closest rushers in FP/touch are Jordan Washington (1.57) and Oregon battering ram Jordon Davison (1.45).

12 - The most efficient rushing quarterback with 50+ pass attempts last season was Texas Tech's Will Hammond, who averaged 6.95 yards per rush last year.

13 - Mississippi State phenom Kamario Taylor leads all such returnees in fantasy production, averaging .93 points per touch. Taylor could be a supernova if he can improve upon his 1.4% plus throw rate.

14 - Georgia QB Gunnar Stockton led all P4 signal callers with a 65% YAC rate on an 8.0 ADOT (59th in P4) as OC Mike Bobo prefers to get his receivers the ball in space rather than hunt downfield.

15 - Iowa State-to-Penn State QB Rocco Becht leads all returnees in both air yard % (63.7%) and Plus Throw Rate (24.1%). He's barely being drafted in Yahoo Standard leagues despite Penn State playing arguably the easiest schedule in the Big 10.

16 - In 2025, 23 RBs scored 10+ rushing TDs. Of those 23, only 14 return to college football (12 to their 2025 teams). Lacy is the only returning P4 RB to score over 20 TDs.

17 - Only 18 returning RBs finished with 20+ receptions in 2025. Of the top-10 ranked RBs in Yahoo, four finished with over 30 receptions in 2025.

For his part, the powerful Baugh closed strong, following former HC Billy Napier's dismissal, recording 17+ fantasy points in his last six contests and earning at least three targets per game in nine of his last 10 appearances.

18 - Of those four runners, only two finished with over 1.20 yards per route run.

19 - In the seven games where he managed to play a full complement of snaps, Minnesota RB Darius Taylor scored 20+ points in five of them. In the other two he still posted respectable 13.7 points against Oregon and 15.9 vs. Purdue.

20 - Dierre Hill only had 90 total touches in 2025 (74 ATT, 16 recs). He only averaged six touches per game, but still finished with an impressive 792 total yards. Hill is one of only two returning RBs with 70+ carries to finish with a breakaway percentage (carries of 15+ yards) of over 60%.

21 - Of the 12 returning P4 wideouts with over 90 targets, only four finished with a reception rate over 70%.

Of those four receivers, only two had an ADOT over 10.0 yards.

Que'Sean Brown transferred from Duke-to-Virginia Tech, and is barely being drafted in Yahoo Standard Leagues, while Smith is Julio Jones 2.0 and a top-three overall selection.

22 - Trinidad Chambliss, Marcel Reed, Arch Manning, Demond Williams and Bear Bachmeier are the only returning P4 QBs to throw for over 3,000 yards and run for over 500 yards. Arch Manning, Conner Weigman and Devon Dampier are the only returning P4 QBs to throw for 20+ TDs and run for 10+ TDs.

23 - Texas A&M's Mario Craver finished the 2025 season at Mississippi State with 85 targets, while KC Concepcion had 101 at A&M. With Concepcion gone to the NFL, Craver has the opportunity to make a massive leap in production in 2026. He finished second among P4 receivers with 3.25 yards per route run, first in yards after catch per reception (9.7), and 10th with 15.5 yards per reception.

24 - NC State RB Hollywood Smothers finished as RB19 among P4 rushers last season on 197 total touches (160 rushing attempts and 37 receptions) in 11 games. He departs for Texas, but RB Duke Scott siphoned 121 touches (106 rushing attempts and 15 receptions) from Smothers and leads the NC State backfield this year. With Smothers gone, Scott has the potential to finish as a top-10 P4 RB.

25 - Kendrick Raphael handled an eye-popping 62% of Cal's rushing opportunities, which was the second-heaviest rushing load in FBS. Raphael hit his stride in ACC play, finishing on a torrid streak scoring 17.5+ points in eight of his last nine games while earning at least four targets in each contest. Last year, SMU HC Rhett Lashlee gave RB1 Tomarion Harden 44% of the team's carries, so it will be interesting to see how heavily Raphael is used in 2026.

26- Texas Tech TE Terrance Carter led all P4 tight ends with 24 tackles on 58 receptions last year for a sterling 43% missed tackle rate. His 24% target share ranked third among returning Power Four tight ends, while his wide-rate alignment ranks top-10. Carter has league-winning upside.

articles.title: Aston Villa: Ollie Watkins transfer saga leaves Villa shellshocked
articles.summary: Ollie Watkins has been an Aston Villa legend but it appears his time at the club is nearing a painful end amid interest from Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
Last year, it was Emi Martinez looking to leave for Manchester United . When asked about the Argentina goalkeeper's absence from last season's opening league match against Crystal Palace , head coach Unai Emery just repeated replacement Marco Bizot's name several times.

Twelve months on, for their Premier League opener at Brighton on Sunday, Ollie Watkins was the name to make Emery bristle.

"This question is for him. I can answer only with my silence," he said, when asked why the striker was not included.

That Villa lost 4-0 - conceding all four in a calamitous opening 31 minutes before having debutant Joao Gomes sent off - merely added to the perceived insult.

Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal have had four offers rejected for Watkins - whose time at Villa now appears to be at a tumultuous end.

Al-Hilal, who have offered close to Â£40m, are not near to Aston Villa 's asking price. As next Tuesday's transfer deadline nears, Villa will play hardball for their all-time record Premier League goalscorer.

A deal is still believed to be some way off, even if Emery revealed last week the striker could leave.

Al-Hilal, who signed Crysensio Summerville from West Ham in July , are likely to need to move one of their overseas players to make room for Watkins, despite loaning Darwin Nunez to Diriyah last week, so there are other moving parts in the deal.

Watkins has been training on his own, having returned from an extended break following the World Cup and is understood to have made his feelings clear to the Villa hierarchy about moving.

There have been no public comments from Watkins or his representatives but he is understood to be open to the move.

They have also kept quiet about Emery's response - particularly his enigmatic "silence" answer to Sky Sports' question on why his striker was not involved at Brighton , which appeared to lay the blame at Watkins' door.

Another unanswered question is whether Villa see the Saudi money for a striker turning 31 in December - and who had been in and out of Emery's team last season - as a good deal.

Perhaps the very real pain at this potential break-up is the reason for the difficulties.

The 30-year-old has 108 goals in 278 games for Villa after joining from Brentford for a then-record Â£28m and has been synonymous with Villa's rise of the past six years.

The triumphant night in Istanbul, when Watkins helped Villa end their 30-year wait for a trophy as they beat Freiburg to win the Europa League, currently stand as a crowning glory.

His departure would be the most emotional of this summer's big exits - as while Ezri Konsa's influence was crucial, Watkins' goals, work-rate and nature made him one of Villa's poster boys.

He is a grounded and family-orientated individual who enjoys the occasional game of golf but always focuses on his football.

But he has been in this position before, although at a lower level.

Having initially been left out by Paul Tisdale at Exeter amid interest from Derby in 2017, he pleaded with the manager to play and came off the bench to score in a win against Wycombe.

Given he has that attitude and desire, those at Villa are surprised at how the relationship with Watkins is ending. It was not expected to be like this.

Had it been someone different, a player who had previously not been a manager's dream to work with, Emery's response might have been more indifferent.

Villa's transfer trouble before deadline

Along with Watkins, Villa must resolve Martinez's future after a second summer of discontent from the Argentina international.

A move to Juventus fell through earlier this month, as they were unwilling to meet Villa's financial demands, and a solution must be found for the 33-year-old after the signing of Zion Suzuki to become the club's number one.

Signing a striker to replace Watkins will be harder than sourcing Konsa's replacement - on which Villa are already working, having had two bids rejected by Southampton for Taylor Harwood-Bellis.

Brian Madjo's availability, after VIlla won their battle against Fifa to register him , gives Emery an additional option, although at 17 the striker cannot be expected to carry the burden.

Villa have been open to letting Tammy Abraham leave but Watkins' increasingly likely departure will have an impact on that thinking.

Striker Abraham, who joined from Besiktas in January, has not been looking for any Villa Park exit and remains happy at the club.

Nicolas Jackson remains a top target for Emery, who worked with the Chelsea forward at Villarreal, while there has been no direct contact with Manchester United over Joshua Zirkzee.

Emery needs to find new heroes after the exits of Morgan Rogers and Youri Tielemans - two Istanbul goalscorers - along with Lucas Digne and Konsa.

But if Watkins goes, his departure will cut the deepest.

articles.title: What to Know About Justin Buzzard, 47-Year-Old Pastor Who Joined CFB Team as DE
articles.summary: They say it's never too late to follow your dreams, and a 47-year-old California pastor is proving just that.
articles.body:
They say it's never too late to follow your dreams, and a 47-year-old California pastor is proving just that.

Justin Buzzard is set to join the San Jose City College Jaguars as a defensive end, nearly 30 years after he last played in a college football game.

"No one's going easy on me... and I'm not going easy on them," Justin Buzzard told Fox & Friends First co-host Todd Piro. "I'm giving them everything I've got, too."

Buzzard added that he was initially apprehensive about how he would be received in the locker room, but his younger teammates have welcomed him with open arms.

"I was really wondering, 'How are they going to handle… a 47-year-old guy showing up?'" he said. "Are they going to receive me? Are they going to accept me? Will they try to go easy on me? Will they try to attack me? And they've been incredible."

Buzzard said his top goal is to "go the distance" and make it through the entire season. The Jaguars will open the 2026 season on Saturday against College of the Redwoods.

articles.title: 10 biggest storylines entering the 2026 college football season
articles.summary: How will Lane Kiffin do in his first season at LSU? Will the Big Ten continue its dominant run with another title? What's the future of the CFP? Here's what...
articles.body:
With the start of the 2026 college football season officially now just days away, it's a perfect time to refresh yourself on some of the biggest themes that will dominate the season.

Here are 10 of the biggest storylines as we enter the third season of the 12-team College Football Playoff era.

If we're counting recent playoff titles as the ultimate barometer, the Big Ten currently has the upper hand. The league has won the last three national championships with three different teams — Michigan, Ohio State and Indiana.

Will one of those three teams win the title again to extend the streak to four? Can Oregon be the team to make it four in a row?

Perhaps tellingly, AP voters are backing the Big Ten early this season. All 69 first-place votes in the preseason poll went to Big Ten teams . Not a single SEC team received a first-place vote, though the league had seven teams in the top 13 and nine teams in the top 25.

The SEC again has an argument that it's the deeper conference in 2026. Last season, seven teams finished with two or fewer conference losses. The Big Ten had just five such teams and only one other with three conference losses.

But the arguments over conference depth are pretty, well, shallow when one league is hogging all the national titles. The Big Ten's claim to being the best conference in college football will only get stronger with another championship this season.

The 12-team playoff is back for a third season and yes, it looks different once again.

The two main changes prevent repeats of what happened at the end of the 2025 season. Thanks to the rule that put the top five conference champions in the field, ACC champion Duke missed out on the playoff in favor of James Madison.

That rule is gone. Instead, all four power conference champions are guaranteed a spot in the field while the fifth spot for a champion will go to the highest-ranked Group of Six team. The odds of two Group of Six teams getting into the field again are extremely low.

Additionally, Notre Dame is guaranteed a spot in the field if it's in the top 12 in the final CFP rankings. A year ago, the Irish were the first team out of the field when Miami jumped them in the final rankings. But Notre Dame was still in the top 12 even with Miami ahead. Had the rule been in effect in 2025, Notre Dame would have still made the postseason and Miami, which made the national title game, would have been left out.

What will playoff look like in the future?

The rivalry between the SEC and the Big Ten is going to continue throughout the 2026 season in playoff discussions too. The two conferences have all the power when it comes to figuring out the future format of the postseason. And they haven't figured out how to come to an agreement on it.

The Big Ten initially proposed a format that would guarantee it and the SEC more spots than the other power conferences. That idea went nowhere. Now, the Big Ten is in favor of expanding the playoff to 24 teams and has even offered to scrap the Big Ten title game if the playoff doubles in size.

Additionally, a 16-team playoff has been floated with four play-in games ahead of a playoff format that looks like the current 12-team iteration. Does that have any support?

Like last season, the future of the CFP is going to be hotly contested. And guess what? If there's no consensus, the 12-team playoff is going to return for 2027.

After leading Ole Miss to the College Football Playoff in 2025, Lane Kiffin couldn't resist LSU and agreed to join the Tigers before the postseason began. By now, you know that Ole Miss didn't want Kiffin coaching the Rebels in the playoff while also working at a bitter rival and promoted defensive coordinator Pete Golding.

Now, Ole Miss enters the 2026 season with similar national title odds and a higher preseason ranking in the AP Top 25 as Kiffin overhauled LSU's roster. In are former Arizona State QB Sam Leavitt, ex-Colorado OT Jordan Seaton and former Ole Miss edge rusher Princewill Umanmielen, among others.

After firing Brian Kelly following a 24-point home loss to Texas A&M, the Tigers finished 7-6 in 2025. It was the school's sixth-straight season with at least three losses since an undefeated run to the national championship in 2019.

No one rational is asking Kiffin to lead the Tigers to an undefeated season in 2026. But as Ole Miss is again a playoff contender, the Rebels are the bar in his first season in Baton Rouge. Oh, LSU heads to Oxford in Week 3, too. It's hard to think of a bigger revenge game for a home fan base in quite some time.

What will coaching carousel look like in 2026?

The firings of Kelly and James Franklin during the middle of the 2025 season were the start of an especially active coaching cycle. More than 30 FBS schools hired new coaches ahead of the 2026 season.

The coaching carousel can't spin as fast during and after the 2026 season , right?

We can't rule anything out after last year — no one saw Franklin's midseason firing coming at this time a year ago — but all signs point to fewer coaching changes. Coaches like Florida State's Mike Norvell, Wisconsin's Luke Fickell and Baylor's Dave Aranda enter the season with pressure for their teams to put up winning seasons, but with 22 power conference coaches entering either their first or second seasons at their current schools, there likely won't be as much action.

The Pac-12 is reborn with six new members

After two years with just Oregon State and Washington State as its members, the Pac-12 added six teams ahead of the 2026 season.

Most of those teams came from the Mountain West, as Boise State, Colorado State, Fresno State, San Diego State and Utah State came over. Texas State joined from the Sun Belt.

This version of the Pac-12 won't be mistaken for a power conference. It barely has enough teams for a conference championship game. Since there are only eight schools in the league, each team plays another twice in the regular season and those matchups will be finalized before the end of the season.

But despite its limited numbers, this is a league that should compete with the American to be the best non-power conference in football this season. Boise State is one of the Group of Six favorites to make the playoff, and a team like Fresno State or even San Diego State could even make a case for the postseason with a Pac-12 title.

What will North Dakota State do at the top level?

The Mountain West went out and got one of the most successful football programs of the 2000s to help replenish its ranks after the Pac-12 took five of its members.

Longtime FCS powerhouse North Dakota State is now at the top level of college football and no one should be surprised if the Bison compete for the Mountain West title. After all, this is a team that has won nine games against FBS schools over the past 21 seasons.

The conference schedule isn't inviting; the Bison have to travel to Air Force, UNLV, New Mexico and Hawaii. Those are four of the best remaining programs in the Mountain West. But the Bison should get at least one win in those games, and the non-conference schedule is extremely easy. Thanks to an NCAA rule change, North Dakota State is eligible to go to a bowl this season and it'll be a shock if the Bison aren't bowl eligible.

Punts will look a bit different in 2026 and many coaches weren't happy about it. Thanks to an offseason rule change , teams who line up to punt will now have to have at least five players wearing Nos. 50-79 on the line of scrimmage. If they don't, certain conditions will need to be met and any players who are on the line as part of a numbering exception cannot shift before the snap.

The Big Ten's coaches were all apparently against the rule and Iowa's Kirk Ferentz, the punt-friendliest head coach in college football, said there was "no compelling reason" for the rule change.

The rules are likely to prevent teams from designing clever punt fake concepts to confuse their opponents. But let's be real, we don't need fewer punt fakes. We need more of them. Could the changes lead to more blocked punts if returning teams are no longer as scared of a fake as they would have been?

Which school will have a first-year coach bounce?

With 17 power conference coaches in their first year at their new schools, there are bound to be at least a few teams that make a major leap from a disappointing 2025. Who are the likeliest candidates?

After a disaster of a 1-11 season in 2025, Oklahoma State hired North Texas coach Eric Morris. Former UNT QB Drew Mestemaker is now in Stillwater, along with prolific RB Caleb Hawkins. A Week 2 game against Oregon will likely be a loss, but the Cowboys don't play either BYU or Utah and also avoid Arizona. A bowl game is very possible.

UCLA is also in line to improve after a 3-9 season in 2025. The Bruins hired Bob Chesney from James Madison, and RB Wayne Knight followed him to Los Angeles along with a bunch of other former Dukes. A stronger running game is key for UCLA; QB Nico Iamaleava was the team's leading rusher in 2025.

It's time to get used to corporate logos on your favorite team's jersey

If you're a soccer fan, you're probably numb to the sponsor names and logos that are commonplace on the front of jerseys in nearly every league across the globe. If you're a baseball fan, you're probably already glossing over the corporate logos on the sleeve of MLB jerseys, though the helmet sponsorships in the postseason are still a bit weird.

How long will it take to get used to similar branding in college sports? The 2026-27 school year is the first where schools can sell corporate logo space on their jerseys and numerous programs across the country have already inked seven-figure deals. Heck, the Big 12 even has a deal with Monster to plaster the energy drink company's logo on every jersey and playing surface.

The patches are going to look out of place at first, but as the weeks go on, we're inevitably going to get used to them. It stinks that corporatism has invaded another part of college football, but it was also the natural progression as schools turn over every leaf looking for revenue-generating opportunities.

articles.title: Manchester City transfer news: Enzo Maresca's side agree deal for Palmeiras winger Allan Elias
articles.summary: Manchester City agree to sign winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a deal worth up to Â£34.2m.
articles.body:
Manchester City have agreed to sign winger Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a deal worth up to Â£34.2m.

The 22-year-old Brazilian will come in as a replacement for compatriot Savinho, who looks set to join Tottenham .

City are set to pay a fixed fee of Â£32m, plus Â£2.2m in add-ons, and a medical is scheduled to take place in the coming days.

They remain in advanced talks to sell Egypt forward Omar Marmoush to Spurs, and sources with knowledge of the situation say there is a "good chance" the deal gets completed before the 1 September transfer deadline.

Discussions are ongoing between the two clubs and there are some details yet to be agreed.

Midfielder Nico Gonzalez may also depart Etihad Stadium before the end of the transfer window, with strong interest in the Spaniard from Newcastle .

articles.title: Troy Deeney's Team of the Week: Trafford, Mendy, Guehi, Palmer, Pedro
articles.summary: After every round of Premier League matches this season, Troy Deeney gives us his team of the week. Do you agree with his choices?
articles.body:
After every round of Premier League matches this season, BBC football pundit Troy Deeney will give you his team and manager of the week.

Do you agree? Give us your thoughts using the comments form at the bottom of this page.

James Trafford ( Leeds ): It's been a big-pressure move for Trafford going to Leeds . I think at the World Cup with England he thought, 'I should be playing more' and he obviously didn't get the time and needed a move away. He produced a strong performance for Leeds at Nottingham Forest and was one of the few goalkeepers to keep a clean sheet.

Keane Lewis-Potter ( Brentford ) : He was excellent defensively and attacking wise and got his goal. He is one of Brentford 's underrated players and sort of sums up their team. Nobody speaks about him or Brentford but they hammered Tottenham .

Nobel Mendy ( Hull City ) : He was so good and powerful. He offered so much defensively to Hull and scored their second goal. He was a real powerhouse. Hull will definitely need him and he is one of those defenders where you think, 'I don't want to play against him'.

Maxence Lacroix ( Chelsea ) : Lacroix just added a level of experience and calmness to Chelsea and also got an assist. He read the game and understood what was needed and provided the maturity that will add so much to Chelsea going forward. It was a very good debut for the France defender.

Maxim de Cuyper ( Brighton ) : He scored, had an assist and was excellent for Brighton . Opponents Aston Villa were poor, but if you watched the first 20 minutes you would see he was really aggressive and really set the tone with the pressure.

Marc Guehi (Man City) : I'll have Guehi in as my holding midfielder. He should have scored two against Bournemouth because he missed a massive chance before he ended up scoring. But he got the equaliser and offered a lot more of a calming presence than City's Â£116m record signing Elliot Anderson - Guehi controlled the game a little bit more.

Vitaly Janelt ( Brentford ): He is one of those big, powerful and dominant players who does the basics really well. He mixed that with a goal against Spurs and you don't really speak about him, but he was always the one breaking up play and doing the horrible things really well.

Christos Tzolis ( Arsenal ) : A lot of people are talking about Arsenal and how they're great. That is absolutely true. And so is the bit of business they did bringing this young man in from Club Brugge. So many goals and assists he brings to the team, but also a calming influence and tenacity as well. Look at Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard, he feels to me like both of them in one. He has a lot more output than those guys. He's going to be a beast for this year.

Anthony Elanga ( Newcastle ): Last season I though he was treated poorly by Eddie Howe because he was one that kept being put on the bench, being introduced late or would be the first one to come off. But he showed in a new formation, under a new manager and somebody who believes in him that he can use his pace and power. As a result he looks like a completely different player and he looked happy. He ran past Milos Kerkez like he wasn't there despite the Liverpool left-back having a five-yard start and produced an unbelievable finish for his goal.

Cole Palmer ( Chelsea ) : One we were all talking about, and should've gone to the World Cup with England. Feels like he's got a point to prove, feels like he's been working hard. The injuries from last year skewed everyone's vision. Everything he did at Fulham was positive. Ran forward with pace, looked like he could move. He had those issues with the groin but now he's chopping and turning.

Joao Pedro ( Chelsea ) : My old Watford team-mate and someone who will make everyone question when they said he wasn't good enough. He's going to have a breakout year.

Sergej Jakirovic ( Hull City ) : Tactically brilliant and had a gameplan for Manchester United . His side gave a bit of space away but wouldn't get transitioned on, gave away a lot of cheap fouls. Went forward in the wide areas, crossed it and finished the action. He was very impressive in the Championship last year, spoke well but never got too high or too low. He'll take a few by surprise but I'm concerned they won't have the quality in the team. For now, who cares?

articles.summary: They grow up so fast.
articles.body:
With class starting at the University of Texas, the athletic department posted some amusing first-day-of-school-inspired pictures. One of those pictures was of quarterback Arch Manning, who is starting 16th grade:

Notably, Manning said he wants to be happy with a family when he grows up and is excited for making new friends during the current school season.

Of course, he's also tasked with leading a national championship contender on the football field. The Longhorns start the 2026 campaign on Sept. 5 against Texas State before a highly anticipated showdown with top-ranked Ohio State the following week.

articles.title: Carlos Baleba: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder from Brighton in Â£70m deal
articles.summary: Manchester United sign Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a Â£70m deal.
articles.body:
Manchester United have signed Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a Â£70m deal.

The Old Trafford club have paid an initial Â£65m, plus a potential Â£5m in add-ons, for the 22-year-old, while Brighton have negotiated a sell-on clause.

United targeted Baleba after deciding to strengthen their midfield further following the summer arrivals of Andrey Santos from Chelsea and Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa .

Baleba has signed a five year-contract at Old Trafford, with the option to extend for a further year.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams," he said. "Playing at Old Trafford is always special, but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba's move follows United's shock 2-0 defeat by Hull City in Saturday's Premier League opener, where Santos and Tielemans made their midfield debuts.

United reignited their interest after attempting to sign him last year near deadline day, but were put off by Brighton 's valuation, which was in excess of Â£100m.

Baleba, who joined Brighton from Lille in 2023, is currently sidelined with an ankle injury he picked up during the Seagulls' pre-season training camp in Austria.

He made 112 appearances for Brighton , scoring four times, and 31 in the Premier League last season as they finished eighth to qualify for this season's Conference League.

"Last season was hard," admitted Baleba in a farewell video.

"There was a night against Aston Villa when I came off after 22 minutes. I sat in the dugout and could not lift my head up. You did not boo me. I have thought about that more than you know. You had every reason to and you did not.

"I will be looking for your result every week for the rest of my life. Thank you, Brighton fans."

The move has taken United's summer spending up to Â£153m as they prepare for a return to the Champions League for the first time since the 2023-24 campaign.

"[He is] a huge talent that the club has been trying to follow for a long time." Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Someone that can improve our team and has different qualities to what we already have in the club.

"The expectation is very high but also we know he is a player we need to give time to become an even better version of himself. We are here to help him set [in] as quick as possible and to help us win games."

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window? Published 11 hours ago

What does your Premier League club still need in the transfer window?

United will hope for the 2024-25 version of Baleba rather than last season's because it was his performances in that campaign that attracted them.

We can't know what would have happened if the approach for Mateus Fernandes had been successful, nor if Mason Mount had not suffered the injury in the pre-season game with Paris St-Germain two weeks ago that ruled him out of the Premier League opener.

However, even before Saturday's disappointing loss at Hull it is clear that, despite adding Santos and Tielemans to their midfield ranks, they still lack physicality and power.

In theory, Baleba should solve that issue.

The 22-year-old is strong in possession, covers ground quickly, is good in the air and alert to danger.

Crucially, he also has three years' worth of top-flight experience in England behind him, having moved to Brighton from Lille when he was 19. It gives him the edge on Santos, also 22, and it will be interesting to see whether the pair compete for the same place at the base of Michael Carrick's midfield or if, against the best sides, they might play together.

It will also be fascinating to see if he gets asked to fill in at left-back too.

He has played there before and, unlike Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui - who could also switch sides if Luke Shaw is unavailable - is left-footed.

Paul Pogba is the only midfield player United have signed for more than the Â£70m they are committing to Baleba which, given his age, is a statement in itself.

'Baleba complements United's other midfielders'

Baleba's appeal lies less in creativity and more in his ability to win possession, cover ground and then carry his team forward.

His 2025-26 campaign was quieter than the previous one, but his 2024-25 numbers show why United have tracked him for so long. He ranked fourth among Premier League midfielders for possessions won in the middle third (107) and interceptions (46), was fifth for ball recoveries (197) and seventh for duels won (199).

That defensive output was matched by his ability to progress possession himself.

Baleba averaged 6.7 progressive carries per 90 minutes, with only three qualifying Premier League defensive midfielders recording more, while 2.9 of those carries travelled at least 10 metres.

His athleticism underpins that game as he reached a top speed of 34.5km/h in 2024-25, compared with 30.5km/h for Casemiro, and averaged 8.2 defensive actions per 90.

He is not necessarily the midfielder United would rely on to dictate possession. Only 11.8% of his passes were classed as line-breaking that season and 22.7% travelled forward - both below the average for central and defensive midfielders.

But that may make him complementary to United's other options rather than a direct alternative. Tielemans can provide more of the progressive distribution, while Baleba offers defensive security and the ability to drive through midfield.

Alongside Kobbie Mainoo, he could take on more of the ball-winning and ground-covering work, while a partnership with Santos could allow Baleba greater freedom to operate box to box.

That versatility is reflected in his positioning as he spent 88% of his minutes last season as a defensive midfielder and 12% in central midfield, suggesting he can anchor the side or step forward depending on who plays alongside him.

United most commonly defended in a 4-2-2-2 last season under Carrick, accounting for 55.9% of their out-of-possession shapes. Baleba's dynamism could be especially valuable in a system where central midfielders are asked to defend large spaces and stop counter-attacks.

There may, however, be an adaptation period.

Baleba is recovering from an ankle ligament injury suffered in pre-season and will need time to recover his match sharpness.

United have also looked to spend longer spells in possession under Carrick, progressing through midfield with quick combinations. Baleba's game is better suited to more open contests, but his passing profile suggests he may need time to adjust to greater responsibility in build-up.

His left foot and mobility should still make him a natural partner for players such as Tielemans or Bruno Fernandes. There is development ahead of him at 22, not least after last season's dip, but at his best Baleba combines defensive activity with the acceleration and carrying power to transform a turnover into an attack within seconds.

articles.title: Man Utd transfer news: Will Michael Carrick's side buy a left-back before transfer window closes?
articles.summary: After spending Â£155m on three midfielders, now Manchester United must decide whether to try to buy a left-back
articles.body:
The signing of Carlos Baleba completes a Â£155m summer revamp of Manchester United's midfield.

At the end of last season, midfield was targeted as a priority area as United looked to build on qualification for the Champions League after a two-year absence.

Baleba arrives along with Andrey Santos, a Â£48m signing from Chelsea, and Â£35m former Aston Villa man Youri Tielemans.

It means that, along with England's Kobbie Mainoo, United now have a spread of different attributes across their four-man midfield, three of whom are 22 or younger.

But, at Manchester United, one bad result brings intense pressure.

Even Michael Carrick's calm exterior cracked in a post-match exchange with former Middlesbrough and Swindon Town forward Jan Aage Fjortoft, now a TV presenter for Viaplay, following the shock defeat at Hull when the Norwegian suggested there was a lack of passion in United's ranks.

"Come on, that's ridiculous," replied Carrick. "You played football. You understand. That's a ridiculous thing to say."

So, now the midfield is sorted, it is natural for fans to look at the other areas of Carrick's squad that could do with reinforcements; namely left-back.

Baleba completes Â£70m Man Utd move from Brighton Published 11 hours ago

Baleba completes Â£70m Man Utd move from Brighton

Signing an additional left-back has looked an obvious thing for Manchester United to do.

Luke Shaw started all 38 Premier League games last season. He started at Hull. Of United's past 44 league games, the 31-year-old England international has failed to start just one, the final game of the 2024-25 campaign, four days after the Europa League final defeat by Tottenham â and he went on the post-season tour of Asia immediately afterwards.

But, before that, Shaw's injury record had not been great.

Between February 2024 and April 2025, he played as many games for England (three) as he did for his club. He missed three months at the start of the 2023-24 campaign.

There were calf and hamstring issues but also a feeling Erik ten Hag rushed him back too quickly.

More than anyone, Shaw benefited from a 40-game season, allowing him to prepare properly, largely for one game a week, sometimes not even that.

That preparation time will not be repeated.

Although there are blank midweeks between Manchester United's first three games, if they get through two EFL Cup rounds, they will not have a full midweek without a game, other than during international breaks, until the one that includes Christmas Day.

It is the combination of Shaw's injury record and the crush of games that has led to the feeling another left-back will arrive.

There is no doubt the club like Newcastle's Lewis Hall. At 21, he is the right age profile and ideally suited to challenging Shaw for his place, with the safety net of there being enough games to keep both men happy.

However, Newcastle don't want to sell. It would take a huge offer to persuade them otherwise and Manchester United's powerbrokers have proved on numerous occasions this summer they will not be held to ransom, or overpay, for players.

In addition, how much money do they have to spend?

In published third-quarter financial accounts to 31 March, United confirmed they owed Â£405.75m in outstanding transfer fees, Â£171.14m of which was due after more than one year. The club are still to outline what the additional $125m (Â£91.64m) they borrowed in a wider refinancing announced in June will be used for.

The assumption is Â£70m for Baleba, equal the sum United paid for Casemiro in 2022 and a figure only exceeded in their history in terms of midfielders by the club record Â£89m spent on Paul Pogba, is at the top end of what they wanted to pay.

Plenty of alternative left-backs to Hall have been mentioned.

Racing Santander's 19-year-old Jorge Salinas has a â¬16m (Â£13.7m) release clause, but is also coveted by Atletico Madrid.

Barcelona's Alejandro Balde was left out of the 5-0 La Liga victory over Elche by coach Hansi Flick, to allow him to "clear his mind" amid intense transfer speculation, with United among those to be linked with the 22-year-old Spain international. Barcelona are said to value him between â¬30m (Â£25.66m) and â¬40m (Â£34.22m).

With a week to go before the transfer window closes, the situation is thought to be fluid, but caution in United circles around the expectations of a new left-back being signed is being stressed.

A significant sale could change the dynamic.

However, the idea of Marcus Rashford leaving has virtually been ruled out with confirmation he will wear the coveted number nine shirt this season, while the anticipated exit of Manuel Ugarte had to be scrapped when he was injured at the World Cup.

Of Carrick's senior squad, forward Joshua Zirkzee appears surplus to requirements, yet with fitness doubts over Amad Diallo â the club are choosing to offer no clarification on the extent of his injury amid a report he could be out for up to six weeks â it is uncertain whether interest from Serie A will lead to a sale.

Carrick does have options at left-back without bringing anyone else in. Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui have both switched flanks in the past, while Baleba, a left-footed player, has played at full-back for Brighton previously.

In addition, Harry Amass was Shaw's back-up during pre-season and the 19-year-old remains at United. But he was not included in Carrick's squad for the Hull trip and the expectation has been he will leave, either permanently or on loan.

Most still think there will be another left-back in Carrick's squad when the transfer window closes on 1 September â but it is by no means certain.

Baleba arrives along with Andrey Santos, a Â£48m signing from Chelsea, and Â£35m former Aston Villa man Youri Tielemans.

articles.title: Liam Delap transfer: Nottingham Forest agree club-record deal to sign Chelsea striker
articles.summary: Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea; striker moved to Stamford Bridge last summer, but scored just two goals in 41 games for the club; Chelsea could make a £20m profit having signed the 23-year-old for £30m
articles.body:
Nottingham Forest have agreed a club-record £50m deal to sign Liam Delap from Chelsea.

The transfer is understood to be worth at least £45m, which could reach £50m with add-ons.

The striker is scheduled to have a medical on Wednesday.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Forest news & transfers🔴⚪
  • Forest fixtures & scores | FREE Forest highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Delap had interest from a number of other Premier League clubs, including Everton, but Forest have secured his signing.

Chelsea signed Delap last summer for £30m from Ipswich and valued him at around £50m this summer.

They could be set for a £20m profit on a striker who scored two goals in 41 appearances last season.

Forest's previous record transfer saw Omari Hutchison join for £37.5m from Ipswich Town in August 2025.

Sherwood backs Forest's Delap move

Tim Sherwood speaking on Soccer Special:

"We know Liam's got the ability; he's shown that in the past. He needs to play on a regular basis now. He needs to stay fit.

"It never worked out at Chelsea. I never think he ever got a run in the team to give that striker the confidence; you need the manager to love you and play you every week, even if you're not playing well. I think he'll get that with Glasner - you've seen that with (Jean-Philippe Mateta) at Palace.

"He [Forest boss Oliver Glasner] likes to play with a big striker; he likes support. If he [Delap] can keep up with play, I think he'll score goals for Nottingham Forest, and I believe he will keep up with play.

"I think he's aggressive; he's got a lot of attributes to be a top, top striker, but Chelsea just did not work for him, and that's what happens.

"Forget about the price tag because the price tags all over the Premier League now are just ridiculous."

What other business could Forest do?

Forest are bringing in Delap to improve their striking options following Taiwo Awoniyi's £9m move to Coventry.

Oliver Glasner's side have been pursuing Tottenham midfielder Lucas Bergvall as an Elliot Anderson replacement, but Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi insists he is staying in north London.

Forest could also add a right wing-back, with Dodo at Fiorentina a player of interest.

Dilane Bakwa is set to join Lille on loan, while centre-backs Zach Abbott and Tyler Bindon could also depart on temporary moves amid interest from Watford.

articles.title: Julian Alvarez transfer latest: Atletico standing firm on Barcelona as Arsenal become only get out for Argentine striker
articles.summary: Julian Alvarez is holding out for a move to Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid are standing firm on the refusal to sell to their LaLiga rivals; Atletico football expert Ruben Uría believes the only way out for Alvarez is to join Premier League champions Arsenal
articles.body:
Julian Alvarez must take one of two paths before the transfer deadline: stay at Atletico Madrid and try to rebuild his connection with the fans or get his head around a potential move to Arsenal.

Atletico have told him again that they will not sell him to Barcelona and that - coupled with the reaction of the club's supporters on Sunday - has left him "devastated", according to well-placed sources in Spain.

The situation is now "extremely tense", according to Atletico expert and journalist Ruben Uría.

"Neither Miguel Gil Marín (CEO of Atlético Madrid) nor the Apollo board want to sell the player to Barcelona," he told Sky Sports News. "The entire Apollo board supports Gil Marín's decision. Alvarez has been told."

According to Uría, Arsenal sporting director Andrea Berta has remained in contact with his former Atletico employers in recent days after Alvarez was booed off by supporters in the opening LaLiga game against Villarreal.

But Arsenal will need Alvarez to put Barcelona out of his mind and show he really wants to join Mikel Arteta's project before any serious negotiations or any offers can be made. In that vein, Arsenal are not currently hopeful of getting him in before September 1 and they are certainly not currently expecting it at the Emirates.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Arsenal news & transfers🔴⚪
  • Arsenal fixtures & scores | FREE Arsenal highlights▶️
  • Got Sky? Watch Premier League games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Latest Sky Sports deals or stream PL games with no contract📺

Alvarez still has his heart set on Barcelona. The question is, will this be the case as the transfer window comes to an end? Will the deadline have any effect? Arsenal will always be ready and open to Alvarez should he change his mind but, at the moment, any move looks very unlikely.

If Alvarez shifts his thinking before the end and pushes for an escape, Atletico are believed to be ready to listen to offers of around £130m (€150m) from Arsenal. Indeed, according to Uría, some people around the Argentine think it is increasingly impossible for him to stay at Atletico given the current atmosphere.

Should Arsenal complete a deal for Alvarez, it would be the 10th £100m+ signing in Premier League history.

It would also be the fourth this summer, after Morgan Rogers' switch to Chelsea, Elliot Anderson's move to Manchester City and Sandro Tonali joining Tottenham.

Uría also told Sky Sports News: "Julian and his agent believe that everything that's happening is the fault of Gil Marín, Atletico Madrid's CEO, who publicly asked them to say they wanted to leave Atletico.

"For their part, Atletico Madrid argues that Julian already knew how Atletico played under Diego Simeone when he signed for the club, that he knew what contract he was signing and what its clause was, and they deny that Atletico told him he could leave for a direct rival.

"We are waiting to see how events unfold regarding Julian, waiting to see how Arsenal reacts, and if they have genuine interest in the Argentina player. Atletico Madrid will not sell to Barcelona.

"Our information today is that the Julian Alvarez situation has become very tense, and according to several reliable sources, right now, in this crucial week, there are only two paths: stay at Atletico Madrid to fulfil his contract or listen to Arsenal's offer and sign for the London club. Julian will have to make his decision."

articles.title: PFA Awards 2026: Bruno Fernandes and Khadija Shaw win player of the year awards
articles.summary: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw win the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.
articles.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes and Manchester City forward Khadija Shaw have won the Professional Footballers' Associations men's and women's player of the year awards.

Both were previously named the Football Writers' Association men's and women's footballers of the year for the 2025-26 season.

Fernandes, who last season broke the record for the most assists in a single Premier League campaign with 21, is the first United player to win the award since Wayne Rooney in 2010.

It is a second win in three seasons for Shaw, who secured her third consecutive Women's Super League (WSL) golden boot with 21 goals as Man City were crowned champions.

City defender Nico O'Reilly succeeds Morgan Rogers as men's young player of the year, with the versatile 21-year-old cementing his place in the starting XI.

He contributed eight goal involvements (five goals) and nine clean sheets in 34 league outings, scoring twice, and was named player of the match as City beat Arsenal in the League Cup final.

Arsenal 's Olivia Smith retained her crown as the women's young player of the year, becoming only the second player after England international Lauren Hemp, to win the award on multiple occasions.

The Canada international, 22, scored 10 goals in all competitions after joining the Gunners for Â£1m last summer from Liverpool .

Individual success for record-breaker Fernandes

Although it was another trophy-less campaign for Man United, Fernandes enjoyed individual success, surpassing Kevin de Bruyne and Thierry Henry's record of 20 assists in a Premier League campaign.

Fernandes set up his side's opener on the final day of the season against Brighton â and scored their third â to finish 2025-26 with nine goals and 21 assists in 35 league outings. Man City's Rayan Cherki was the second-most prolific provider, with 12 assists.

His haul helped United finish third and secure Champions League football.

In total, the 31-year-old scored nine goals and contributed 22 assists in 37 matches in all competitions.

Fernandes, who joined the club from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020, beat Arsenal trio Gabriel Magalhaes, David Raya, and Declan Rice and Man City attackers Cherki and Erling Haaland to the award.

He is only the second Portuguese to be named player of the year, following back-to-back wins for former Man United winger Cristiano Ronaldo in 2007 and 2008.

Shaw scored 21 goals in 22 appearances as Man City clinched their second WSL title.

The Jamaica international registered hat-tricks against Aston Villa (four goals) and Tottenham and scored twice against West Ham on the final day of the season to become the first player to score 20 or more goals in three different WSL seasons.

Shaw is the first player to win three WSL golden boots, moving clear of two-time winners Vivienne Miedema and Sam Kerr.

The 29-year-old scored a further five goals, including the opener in the final, as Man City won the FA Cup.

Shaw, the third individual to win multiple PFA women's player of the year awards, joining Lucy Bronze and Fran Kirby, previously completed the PFA and FWA double following the 2023-24 campaign.

Team-mate Yui Hasegawa, Aston Villa 's Kirsty Hanson, Chelsea 's Lauren James, Man United's Jess Park, and Arsenal 's Alessia Russo were also shortlisted.

Arsenal and Man City dominate team of the year

The Premier League team of the year, as voted for by the players, was dominated by champions Arsenal and runners-up Man City.

Arsenal only conceded 27 goals last season, with that impressive record reflected in the selections of goalkeeper Raya and defenders Gabriel, William Saliba and Jurrien Timber named alongside midfielder Rice.

Man City have four representatives â O'Reilly, Cherki, Haaland and Antoine Semenyo â with Man United's Fernandes and team of the year debutant Igor Thiago ( Brentford ) completing the XI.

articles.title: Dae'Quan Wright Commits to Lane Kiffin's LSU in CFB Transfer Portal After NFL Stint With Browns
articles.summary: Former Ole Miss and Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright—who recently entered the NCAA transfer portal—has officially cleared waivers and is expected to sign with Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.
articles.body:
Former Ole Miss and Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright—who recently entered the NCAA transfer portal—has officially cleared waivers and is expected to sign with Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Schefter first reported Sunday that Cleveland would waive the tight end, who will join LSU if he clears NFL waivers.

"Wright is believed to be the first player who could play for an NFL team, and then go back to play in college," Schefter added."

Max Olson of ESPN reported Thursday that Wright, former SMU running back TJ Harden, former BYU offensive lineman Weylin Lapuaho, former Ole Miss defensive lineman Zxavian Harris, former James Madison linebacker Trent Hendrick, former Appalachian State cornerback Ethan Johnson and former New Mexico kicker Luke Drzewiecki are entering the portal.

They are able to do so thanks to a temporary restraining order granted by a Louisiana court.

On Wednesday, the Associated Press noted 33 athletes in various sports—including 16 football players—were part of a lawsuit as they sought a fifth year of collegiate eligibility. The temporary restraining order from a Louisiana court made them eligible to return.

Brad Crawford of CBS Sports noted Wright, who has been a member of the Browns' practice squad during training camp, is the first active NFL player to enter the collegiate transfer portal.

While he went undrafted in April, he helped lead Ole Miss to a College Football Playoff spot in his final season with 39 catches for 635 yards and five touchdowns.

He scored one of his touchdowns during an SEC win over South Carolina and another during the Rebels' CFP loss to Miami in the national semifinals.

Harris was also part of that Ole Miss team and finished the 2025 season with 58 tackles, nine tackles for loss, three sacks, three passes defended and one interception.

articles.title: O'Neill takes responsibility with nowhere to hide for Celtic
articles.summary: Celtic manager Martin O'Neill says his team have a "million miles to go" after defeat in Austria.
articles.body:
In the open air of the Raiffeisen Arena, with bedlam all around, there was nowhere to hide for Celtic or Martin O'Neill.

The Scottish champions had endured one of the darkest nights in their European history.

After going out to Kairat Almaty on penalties last year at this stage of the Champions League play-offs, that is saying something.

Four goals up on aggregate against LASK, O'Neill's Celtic somehow conspired to implode in a second half with little sign of a response on the way to a 5-4 aggregate loss following extra time.

There was no hiding place, and the Celtic manager was frank when put in the spotlight at full-time.

"I'm responsible for this one," he said.

"Without a doubt. Naturally it took me a long time to get over the Uefa Cup final in 2003 but this was majorly disappointing.

"In the context of things, one was a final which it would have been terrific to win, this was a qualifying game which we should have been able to get through.

"We know that we are a million miles from the finished article. That's absolutely true. I think we thought that anyway."

Celtic blow four-goal lead to LASK in Champions League collapse

Exhausted & fragile - how Celtic's capitulation unfolded

O'Neill was not in charge for that defeat in Kazakhstan a year ago as it triggered the start of the end for Brendan Rodgers' second spell at Celtic Park.

The current Parkhead boss helped steady Celtic's ship last term following Rodgers' exit and again following the Wilfried Nancy saga to guide them to another league title and a Scottish Cup.

This season appeared to get off to a prosperous start until the roof began to cave in over in Austria .

Away from the raw pain of stumbling in such a stark way, the aftermath could be telling for Celtic who now have to not only pick themselves up, but finish off a transfer window without the hefty windfall which would have blown in with the Champions League.

"The qualification for the Champions League is major, it's major in every aspect," said O'Neill.

"Financially, for prestige, but we have to pick ourselves up. That's my responsibility again to do that.

"I think I said last week that if you could qualify for the Champions League there would be players wanting to come on that basis.

"That's not going to be the case but we'll see. Tonight we came up well and truly short, particularly in the second half."

Celtic captain Callum McGregor tells Amazon Prime: "We got what we deserved. We were passive all night. We looked scared to go and win the game.

"I didn't think we were that good in the first leg either. We scored at good times and got away with it.

"We have to suck it up. We apologise to our supporters and the club because there's no way we should lose that game.

"It's as much on the players as everyone else. You can't look for excuses elsewhere.

"You'll now see what people are made of. When you play like that you can't have any excuses whatsoever.

"When you go 1-0 up in the game and it still doesn't settle you, you can't have any excuse and that's on us.

"You fall at a big hurdle and these questions [on whether the squad are ready] are going to be asked. You can't lose by that margin then look for excuses elsewhere.

"This is what it's like to play at Celtic. You have to bounce back, you have to show a reaction and that's what Celtic are all about."

Former Celtic captain Scott Brown on BBC Radio Scotland: " It was a fantastic start, you go 1-0 up, but that seems like forever ago. Now they've crashed out the Champions League and conceded five goals.

"LASK outran Celtic in a couple of areas, the two up front were strong, solid and willing runners.

"LASK deserve to go through with that performance. I feel for the lads because I've been in that situation as well."

Former Celtic manager Neil Lennon on Amazon Prime: "It looked to me as if Celtic were exhausted. Fragile in duels. It only looked like there would be one winner.

"They battered Celtic tonight, physically and on the football side. It could have been more."

Former Celtic midfielder Stiliyan Petrov: "Everyone [is to blame].

"They are all in it together. A big club like Celtic should be able to hold that out."
